Gabonreview, citing the newsletter Africa Intelligence, reported that in November 2023 Grand Master Guillaume Trichard met coup leader Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema in Libreville in secret and offered support to his transitional council. It described Oligui as a non-practising Freemason. Trichard also met the council of the Grande Loge symbolique du Gabon, the country's own lodge. Oligui was elected president in April 2025.
cases.cite: Gabonreview, 22 Nov 2023, citing Africa Intelligence
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): A secret meeting offering support to a ruler; nothing placed inside or decided.

cases.n: Michael Flynn was paid for Turkish-interest work before becoming NSA
cases.d: Michael Flynn's consulting firm was paid $530,000 for lobbying work that may have benefited Turkey's government, shortly before he became National Security Adviser, the official who runs the White House's foreign-policy staff. The money came in autumn 2016 from Inovo BV, a company owned by Turkish businessman Ekim Alptekin. Flynn served as National Security Adviser from 22 January to 13 February 2017, and on 8 March 2017 filed a retroactive foreign-agent registration acknowledging the work may have benefited Turkey. His business partner Bijan Kian was convicted of acting as an unregistered agent of Turkey in 2019, but the judge threw out the verdict for insufficient evidence.
cases.cite: Flynn Intel Group FARA registration, US Justice Department, 8 March 2017; US v. Rafiekian (E.D. Va. 2019); Wikipedia 'Michael Flynn'
cases.org_note: Turkish government interests via Inovo BV
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): Paid work before taking office; no decision in office shown serving Turkey.

cases.n: Center for American Progress alumni staff the Biden White House
cases.rank: White House chief of staff, staff secretary, senior advisers, Veterans Affairs secretary
cases.d: The Center for American Progress (CAP), a Washington think tank founded by John Podesta in 2003 as a Democratic counterpart to the Heritage Foundation, supplied many senior Biden-administration officials. They included chief of staff Ron Klain, economic advisers Brian Deese and Gene Sperling, Veterans Affairs Secretary Denis McDonough, Pentagon chief of staff Kelly Magsamen, Neera Tanden (CAP president 2011–21, then White House staff secretary and senior adviser) and John Podesta himself (senior clean-energy adviser). Business Insider counted nearly 70 CAP employees who had left for administration posts by mid-2021. The record shows the staffing route, not specific decisions taken for CAP.
cases.cite: Fox News, 15 September 2022, citing Business Insider (2021); Wikipedia 'Center for American Progress'
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): Record itself says no decisions shown for the think tank.

cases.n: Universal Church bishop Marcelo Crivella: senator, minister, Rio mayor
cases.rank: Mayor of Rio de Janeiro; earlier senator and federal minister of fisheries
cases.d: The Universal Church of the Kingdom of God (IURD), a Brazilian Pentecostal church founded in 1977 by Edir Macedo, has put its bishops into public office. Marcelo Crivella, an IURD bishop and Macedo's nephew, was a senator (2003–2016), Minister of Fishing and Aquaculture under Dilma Rousseff (2012–2014) and mayor of Rio de Janeiro (2017–2020). Police arrested him at home on 22 December 2020, nine days before his term ended, in an investigation into a kickback scheme in his administration, and he was suspended from office. He has sat in the federal Chamber of Deputies since February 2023.
cases.cite: Rio de Janeiro state prosecutors and courts, arrest of 22 December 2020; Wikipedia 'Marcelo Crivella'
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): Individual bishop in office; the kickback arrest is not tied to the church.

cases.n: Atlas Network-trained MBL leader Kim Kataguiri enters Congress
cases.d: The Atlas Network, a US-based network that funds and trains free-market think tanks worldwide, trained activists in Brazil who went on to hold office. In April 2015 Atlas described Kim Kataguiri, head of the Movimento Brasil Livre (MBL), which led street protests against President Dilma Rousseff, as working with its Brazilian partner Estudantes Pela Liberdade, and said 'many members' of the MBL had passed through its training programme. Kataguiri was elected to the federal Chamber of Deputies in 2018 and re-elected in 2022.
cases.cite: Atlas Network, 'Students For Liberty Plays Strong Role in Free Brazil Movement', 1 April 2015
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): Atlas-trained activist elected; no decision shown serving the network.

cases.n: Javier Milei — Atlas Network says its partners shaped his reforms
cases.d: The Atlas Network, a US-based network of free-market think tanks, says its Argentine partner groups helped shape the policies of President Javier Milei, who came up through its circles. Before entering politics Milei won the Liberty Prize of Fundación Atlas in 2018, sat on the advisory board of Fundación Libre and spoke at events of Atlas partners Fundación Libertad y Progreso and Federalismo y Libertad; his adviser Alberto Benegas Lynch is a Mont Pelerin Society director active in several Atlas groups (DeSmog, August 2023). Milei took office in December 2023. In August 2025 the Atlas Network credited Libertad y Progreso, Fundación Libertad and the Asociación Argentina de Contribuyentes with helping push his deregulation, tax and labour reforms; these are the network's own claims.
cases.cite: DeSmog, 22 August 2023; Atlas Network, 'Sharpening Milei's Chainsaw', 29 August 2025
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): Open think-tank advocacy and the network's own claims of influence; no Atlas people shown placed inside or steering decisions.

cases.n: Rafael López Aliaga — Opus Dei member as mayor of Lima
cases.d: Rafael López Aliaga, a member of the Catholic organisation Opus Dei, governed Peru's capital as mayor of Lima. Opus Dei's lay members seek holiness in ordinary work, and it has long had members in Latin American governments. López Aliaga, leader of the Renovación Popular party, describes himself as an Opus Dei member who keeps celibacy. He was mayor from 1 January 2023 until he resigned on 13 October 2025 to run for president; he came third in the April 2026 first round with 11.91% and was elected to the national Senate, taking office in July 2026.
cases.cite: Wikipedia 'Rafael López Aliaga' (Opus Dei membership and offices)
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): Only that the mayor is an Opus Dei member; nothing shows the group steering his decisions.

cases.n: Eduardo Arana — Peru PM's ministry hired a reputed lodge member
cases.rank: President of the Council of Ministers (prime minister); earlier Minister of Justice
cases.d: Peruvian television reported that a Masonic lodge member was hired into Peru's Justice Ministry while a reputed senior Freemason ran it. Freemasonry is a network of private fraternal clubs called lodges; the Scottish Rite is one of its branches, and the 33rd degree is its highest rank. In July 2025 the programme Cuarto Poder reported that Prime Minister Eduardo Arana reportedly holds that degree, and that while he was Justice Minister a lodge member, Elías Falla Villegas, was hired as a consultant in November 2023 at S/15,600 a month. Another reputed lodge member's foundation received an official certification at a July 2024 ceremony Arana attended. Arana said membership of a private association was no grounds to assume favours and that the hire met the job's requirements. No lodge was named.
cases.cite: Canal N, 7 July 2025, citing Cuarto Poder (América TV)
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): A reputed Freemason minister and one lodge member's hire; no lodge named or shown steering the ministry.

cases.n: Sanae Takaichi — Nippon Kaigi Diet league member becomes PM
cases.d: Sanae Takaichi, a member of the parliamentary league of the nationalist lobby Nippon Kaigi, became Japan's prime minister in October 2025. Nippon Kaigi (Japan Conference) is Japan's largest nationalist lobby group, founded in 1997, with about 38,000–40,000 members; it works on politicians through a cross-party league of members of the Diet, Japan's parliament. Takaichi has served in that league, as The Japan Times reported in 2021. She won the Liberal Democratic Party leadership in October 2025 and was elected prime minister by the Diet on 21 October 2025, at the head of an LDP–Japan Innovation Party coalition. She still holds the office.
cases.cite: The Japan Times, 5 September 2021; Wikipedia summary of Nippon Kaigi and of Takaichi's election
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): Only that the prime minister sits in Nippon Kaigi's Diet league; no decision shown steered by it.

cases.n: Takaichi cabinet — five ministers with Unification Church ties
cases.d: Five ministers in Sanae Takaichi's first cabinet had ties to the Unification Church (Family Federation for World Peace and Unification), a Korean-founded church whose links to lawmakers of the governing Liberal Democratic Party came to light after Shinzo Abe's killing in 2022; Tokyo courts ordered its Japanese branch dissolved in 2025. Japan Press Weekly (Akahata) reported on 23 October 2025 that Matsumoto Yohei's party branch paid dues to the church-linked Women's Federation for World Peace (revealed in 2019); Ueno Kenichiro paid fees to affiliated bodies in 2018–19 and attended an affiliated lawmakers' meeting in 2021; Akazawa Ryosei and Ishihara Hirotaka spoke at affiliated meetings; and Kiuchi Minoru sent a congratulatory telegram to an affiliated company's event in 2018.
cases.cite: Japan Press Weekly (Akahata), 23 October 2025
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): Ties are small dues, fees, speeches and a telegram; nothing shows the church steering the ministers.

cases.n: Unification Church papers say it backed 290 LDP lawmakers in 2021
cases.d: Documents of the Unification Church, a Korean-founded church, say it backed 290 members of Japan's governing Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) in the October 2021 lower-house election. The documents were seized in South Korean investigations, and in January 2026 South Korean media reported that Eiji Tokuno, then head of the church's Japan branch, gave that figure to church leader Han Hak-ja in a report. The LDP's own 2022 survey had found 179–180 of its lawmakers with ties to the church. The same documents are reported to describe Abe as pleased with church support at a meeting before the 2019 upper-house election. Akahata separately reported that an August 2021 'TM Special Report' to Han said Takaichi becoming LDP president would be 'Heaven's greatest wish fulfilled'.
cases.cite: Jiji Press, 2 January 2026, citing South Korean media; Akahata/Japan Press Weekly, January 2026
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): Electoral backing of LDP candidates from outside; the record shows no decisions inside government made for the church.

cases.n: China-funded Solomon Islands PM's fund paid 39 of 50 MPs
cases.d: Money from China, paid into a fund controlled by the Solomon Islands prime minister's office, went to 39 of the country's 50 MPs weeks before a vote on removing him. China agreed in 2019 to fund this discretionary fund, as Taiwan had done before. At a livestreamed parliamentary budget committee hearing in August 2022, the prime minister's secretary Jimmy Rodgers said China had provided SBD20.9 million (about US$2.49 million) spent in 2021, and that the MPs received payments in two tranches, on 22 November and 13 December 2021. Sogavare survived a no-confidence vote in December 2021; opposition leader Matthew Wale accused him of using the money to stay in power, which Sogavare's office denied.
cases.cite: Parliamentary budget committee hearing, August 2022 (Reuters via VOA, 25 August 2022)
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): China openly funded a fund the prime minister controlled; the record does not show China directing the payments to MPs.

cases.n: Huang Jing — Singapore expels professor as foreign agent of influence
cases.rank: foreign-policy academic (target: Singapore foreign policy and opinion)
cases.d: Singapore's government says a foreign intelligence service used a professor at its state university's public-policy school to influence Singapore's foreign policy. On 4 August 2017 the Ministry of Home Affairs cancelled the permanent residence of Huang Jing, a US-citizen professor at the National University of Singapore's Lee Kuan Yew School of Public Policy, and of his wife, and banned both from re-entering. The ministry called him 'an agent of influence of a foreign country' who worked with that country's intelligence agents to influence Singapore's foreign policy and public opinion. It did not name the country. Huang denied the charge.
cases.cite: Singapore Ministry of Home Affairs statement, 4 August 2017
cases.org_note: prc_state is used because the case is widely read as China, but Singapore's ministry did not name the country
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): An agent of influence working through an academic post and public opinion, not placed inside a government body.

cases.n: Chen Zhi — alleged scam-empire boss served as Hun Sen's adviser
cases.rank: adviser to Hun Sen and other leaders
cases.d: Chen Zhi, whom US prosecutors call the head of a cyber-fraud empire run from scam compounds, served as an official adviser to Cambodia's top leaders. Born in Fujian, China, he took Cambodian citizenship in 2014 and built the Prince Group, one of Cambodia's largest conglomerates. He held the honorary title Neak Oknha, and advised Hun Sen, interior minister Sar Kheng and National Assembly president Heng Samrin. On 14 October 2025 the US Justice Department indicted him for fraud and money laundering and seized about 127,271 bitcoin (about US$14 billion), while the US and UK sanctioned 146 people and firms linked to the group. In January 2026 Cambodia said it had arrested him, revoked his citizenship and sent him to China to face charges.
cases.cite: US Department of Justice indictment and OFAC/UK sanctions, 14 October 2025; Cambodian government statement, January 2026
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): The scam-group boss held an advisory title, but no decision is shown that served his group.

cases.n: C. P. Radhakrishnan — RSS member since 16, now Vice President
cases.d: C. P. Radhakrishnan, a member of the Hindu nationalist Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS) since the age of 16, became Vice President of India in 2025. He was also active in the RSS's earlier political wing, the Bharatiya Jana Sangh, and later served as a BJP MP for Coimbatore and as governor of several states. He was elected the 15th Vice President and took office on 12 September 2025. The vice president also chairs the upper house of Parliament, the Rajya Sabha.
cases.cite: Wikipedia: C. P. Radhakrishnan (citing Indian press)
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): Only that the vice-president is a long-time RSS member; no decision shown steered by the RSS.

cases.n: Fight Impunity — NGO used as channel for Qatar and Morocco cash
cases.rank: former MEP and chair of the EP human rights subcommittee
cases.d: Belgian prosecutors say Morocco's foreign intelligence agency (DGED) paid a former member of the European Parliament to lobby for Morocco there, and that a Brussels charity was used to route foreign payments. Fight Impunity was a human-rights NGO founded by former Italian MEP Pier Antonio Panzeri, who had chaired the Parliament's human rights subcommittee. Police found about €600,000 in cash at his home in December 2022. Prosecutors say the DGED agreed in 2019 to pay Panzeri and his former assistant Francesco Giorgi €50,000 a year each. Giorgi told investigators that payments from Qatar and Mauritania were routed through the NGO. Panzeri signed a plea deal with Belgian prosecutors in January 2023 to tell what he knew.
cases.cite: Belgian Federal Prosecutor's Office; Panzeri plea agreement, January 2023; Financial Times and Der Spiegel reporting on the case file
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): The record shows a former MEP paid to lobby and an NGO used to route money, not anyone inside the Parliament (the sitting MEPs appear in other entries).

cases.n: Salvini associate negotiated secret Russian oil money for the Lega
cases.rank: party (Lega) – aide to deputy prime minister Matteo Salvini
cases.d: A close associate of Matteo Salvini, leader of Italy's Lega party, negotiated with Russians over an oil deal meant to channel Russian money illegally into the party. At an October 2018 meeting at the Metropol hotel in Moscow, Gianluca Savoini, president of the Lombardy–Russia cultural association, discussed the deal; a recording of the meeting was published in 2019. Milan prosecutors investigated Savoini and others for international corruption. In April 2023 a Milan judge closed the case: the judge found the actions were 'unequivocally aimed' at illegally financing the party, but the deal never reached the point where it could achieve that.
cases.cite: Milan Public Prosecutor's Office investigation; dismissal order of the Milan preliminary-investigations judge, April 2023
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): Talks to fund a party secretly; a party is not a government body, and no official is alleged to have acted for Russia.

cases.n: Frank Creyelman — Flemish ex-senator paid by China's spy agency
cases.rank: former Belgian senator and Flemish MP (Vlaams Belang)
cases.d: An officer of China's Ministry of State Security, its main spy agency, paid Frank Creyelman, a Belgian politician, to influence debate in Europe for three years. Creyelman had sat in the Belgian Senate (1999–2007) and the Flemish Parliament (2007–2014) for Vlaams Belang. A joint investigation by the Financial Times, Der Spiegel and Le Monde reported the payments on 15 December 2023. Vlaams Belang expelled him; Belgian police investigated but reported that a gap in Belgian criminal law prevented prosecution.
cases.cite: Financial Times / Der Spiegel / Le Monde joint investigation, 15 December 2023; Vlaams Belang expulsion
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): The payments came after he had left both parliaments; the record shows no one inside an institution.

cases.n: Ye Jianming — Chinese 'friendship' body veteran advised Czech president
cases.rank: economic adviser to President Miloš Zeman
cases.d: Czech President Miloš Zeman made Ye Jianming, a former officer of a Beijing 'friendship' body, his economic adviser. The China Association for International Friendly Contact (CAIFC) is a body that builds contacts with foreigners on China's behalf. Ye was its deputy secretary-general from 2003 to 2005 and chairman of the oil conglomerate CEFC China Energy. Zeman made him an economic adviser (from 2015 per some sources, January 2017 per others) while CEFC bought Czech assets. Ye was detained in China in March 2018 and Shanghai state investors took over CEFC.
cases.cite: Czech Presidential Office statements; Reuters and Fortune reporting on CEFC
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): A China-linked businessman held an adviser title, but no decision is shown that served China or his company.

cases.n: French state report alleges Muslim Brotherhood entry into local politics
cases.d: A French government report says the Muslim Brotherhood, an Islamist movement founded in Egypt in 1928, works its way into French local politics. In May 2025 the report, by two senior civil servants and commissioned by the government, was examined by President Macron's Defence Council. It called the Brotherhood a 'threat to national cohesion', said 'political Islamism' was spreading 'from the bottom up' at municipal level, and named the federation Musulmans de France (formerly UOIF) as the Brotherhood's national branch. The authors also wrote that no recent document showed a wish by Muslims in France to set up an Islamic state. Musulmans de France rejected the findings.
cases.cite: French government report on the Muslim Brotherhood and political Islamism, Defence and National Security Council, 21 May 2025
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): A general claim of spread into local politics; the record does not say who got inside which institution.

cases.n: Jorge Fernández Díaz — Opus Dei member as Spain's interior minister
cases.d: Jorge Fernández Díaz, reported to be a member of the Catholic institution Opus Dei, ran Spain's police and Guardia Civil as interior minister from 2011 to 2016. Opus Dei's lay 'supernumerary' members follow its spiritual programme while working in ordinary jobs. Fernández Díaz, a Partido Popular politician, served in Mariano Rajoy's government and is reported to be a supernumerary.
cases.cite: Spanish press reporting compiled in Wikipedia biography
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): Only that the minister is reported to be an Opus Dei member; no decision shown steered by it.

cases.n: Paola Binetti — Opus Dei numerary in Italy's parliament
cases.rank: Senator and member of the Chamber of Deputies (from 2006)
cases.d: Paola Binetti, a celibate 'numerary' member of the Catholic institution Opus Dei, sat in Italy's parliament from 2006. Numeraries live in Opus Dei's centres. Binetti, a psychiatrist and professor at the Opus Dei-founded Campus Bio-Medico University in Rome, was latterly a senator elected in 2018, for The Daisy, the Democratic Party and then the Union of the Centre. She has said publicly that she is a numerary and wears a cilice, a spiked band worn as penance.
cases.cite: Italian Senate member record; Binetti's own public statements
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): Only that the legislator is an Opus Dei numerary; no decision shown steered by it.

cases.n: Ex-EU commissioner Kroes lobbied Dutch leaders for Uber
cases.d: Neelie Kroes, the EU's digital commissioner until 2014, helped the US ride-hailing company Uber lobby Dutch politicians, including Prime Minister Mark Rutte, during her 18-month cooling-off period, the rule that limits former commissioners' work for companies. Commission President Jean-Claude Juncker had refused her request to work for Uber formally. The help came to light in the Uber Files, internal Uber documents leaked and published in July 2022. Kroes denies wrongdoing.
cases.cite: The Guardian / ICIJ, 'The Uber Files', July 2022
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): A former commissioner lobbying national leaders from outside; no one inside shown working for Uber.

cases.n: SNC-Lavalin: Trudeau pressed attorney general on company's behalf
cases.d: SNC-Lavalin (now AtkinsRéalis), a Montreal engineering company facing bribery charges over Libya, got Canada's prime minister to act for it inside government. It lobbied for a law allowing deferred prosecution deals (agreements that let a company avoid trial), holding 51 meetings with officials and MPs over about 20 months. When prosecutors refused SNC such a deal, Prime Minister Justin Trudeau pressed Attorney General Jody Wilson-Raybould to overrule them. On 14 August 2019 Ethics Commissioner Mario Dion found Trudeau had broken section 9 of the Conflict of Interest Act, which bars officials from improperly furthering another person's interests. The company later pleaded guilty to fraud and was fined C$280 million (December 2019).
cases.cite: Conflict of Interest and Ethics Commissioner, 'Trudeau II Report', 14 Aug 2019
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): Open lobbying from outside; the record does not show the company's people inside or officials secretly working for it.

cases.n: Odebrecht money in Peru's Humala campaigns; 15-year sentences
cases.d: Peruvian prosecutors argued that Odebrecht, the Brazilian construction group at the centre of Latin America's largest bribery case, and the Venezuelan government financed Ollanta Humala's 2006 and 2011 presidential campaigns. On 15 April 2025 a Lima court convicted Humala, president from 2011, and his wife Nadine Heredia of money laundering linked to Odebrecht and sentenced each to 15 years. Money laundering here means hiding the source of illegal funds. Heredia left for Brasília after Brazil granted her diplomatic asylum. Both deny the charges.
cases.cite: Peru, National Superior Court of Specialized Criminal Justice, 15 Apr 2025
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): Campaign financing convicted as money laundering; the record shows no decision in office made for Odebrecht or Venezuela.

cases.n: Gates Foundation money steers WHO programmes
cases.d: The Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, a private US charity, funds the World Health Organization (WHO), the UN's health agency, in a way that lets it choose what the money is spent on. In 2020 it was the WHO's second-largest contributor; in the period cited it gave 45% of the WHO's funds from non-state bodies, about 12% of WHO operating spending. Most of this money is earmarked, meaning it can only be used for programmes the foundation picks. Academics and charities have warned that this can tilt WHO priorities toward the foundation's own.
cases.cite: WHO contributor data as summarised by Wikipedia
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): Earmarked funding given openly from outside; no Gates people shown placed inside the WHO.

cases.n: IMF staffer made Pakistan's central bank chief during bailout talks
cases.rank: Governor of the State Bank of Pakistan
cases.d: Reza Baqir, a staff member of the International Monetary Fund (IMF), was appointed Governor of the State Bank of Pakistan on 4 May 2019 while Pakistan was negotiating an IMF bailout. The IMF lends to countries in crisis on condition that they change their policies, and a central bank governor sets interest rates and manages the currency, both points in such talks. Baqir had been the IMF's mission chief for Romania and Bulgaria. He was appointed a day after his predecessor was abruptly removed, Reuters reported. He served until 4 May 2022.
cases.cite: Government of Pakistan appointment, 4 May 2019 (Reuters)
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): An IMF staffer took the central bank post, but no decision is shown that served the IMF.

cases.n: World Bank managing director became Nigeria's finance minister
cases.rank: Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister for the Economy
cases.d: Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala moved from the World Bank, which lends to Nigeria, into the Nigerian ministry that deals with it. She had a 25-year career at the Bank and was a managing director from December 2007 to 2011. President Goodluck Jonathan appointed her finance minister and coordinating minister for the economy on 17 August 2011, a post she held until May 2015. She became Director-General of the World Trade Organization in March 2021 and was reappointed in November 2024.
cases.cite: Nigerian presidential appointment, 17 Aug 2011; WTO General Council decisions 2021 and 2024
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): A World Bank official became finance minister, but no decision is shown that served the Bank.

cases.n: China-linked hackers inside UN aviation agency; evidence hidden
cases.d: Hackers most likely from Emissary Panda, a group tied to the Chinese government, broke into the systems of the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) in November 2016 and used them to infect visitors, CBC reported in February 2019 from internal documents. ICAO is the UN agency that sets world aviation standards. CBC said ICAO's IT staff and their supervisor tried to hide evidence, and sources said Secretary General Fang Liu, a Chinese national, shelved recommendations to investigate them. ICAO disputed the account. The US ambassador to ICAO later called the handling 'unacceptable'.
cases.cite: CBC News investigation, Feb 2019
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): A hack from outside; the record does not show the officials who hid evidence were working for China.

cases.n: FIFA president met Swiss attorney general in secret during FIFA probe
cases.d: FIFA, world football's governing body, based in Zurich, got private access to the head of the Swiss prosecution service while that service was investigating corruption at FIFA. Its president, Gianni Infantino, held unrecorded meetings in 2016 and 2017 with Michael Lauber, Switzerland's attorney general. Lauber was found to have misled the body that oversees federal prosecutors about the meetings, in a 2020 ruling of the Swiss Federal Administrative Court, and he left office that year. A special prosecutor opened a criminal case against Infantino over the meetings; it was closed without charges on 26 October 2023.
cases.cite: Swiss Federal Administrative Court ruling 2020; Swiss special prosecutor decision, 26 Oct 2023 (AP)
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): Secret meetings between FIFA's president and the attorney general; the record does not allege any prosecution decision made for FIFA.

cases.n: La Línea: customs bribery ring reached Guatemala's president
cases.d: 'La Línea', a bribery ring inside Guatemala's customs service, reached Vice-President Roxana Baldetti and President Otto Pérez Molina. It was exposed in 2015 by Guatemala's Public Ministry (the prosecution service) and CICIG, an international commission set up by a 2006 UN–Guatemala agreement to help prosecutors take apart criminal networks inside the state. Congress lifted Pérez Molina's immunity 132–0 and he resigned on 2 September 2015. On 7 December 2022 both were sentenced to 16 years; Pérez Molina was released on bond in January 2024.
cases.cite: Guatemala, Sentencing Court, 7 Dec 2022; Congress vote 1 Sept 2015
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): A bribery ring run by the state's own officials; no outside party got inside.

cases.n: Tony Blair Institute advisers placed inside Rwanda's government
cases.rank: Office of the President / Prime Minister (strategy and delivery units)
cases.d: The Tony Blair Institute for Global Change, a London-based non-profit founded by the former UK prime minister, places its advisers inside governments. In Rwanda it has supported a Strategy and Policy Unit and a Government Action Coordination Unit and worked on Imihigo, a system of performance contracts for officials; in Kenya it supported a Presidential Delivery Unit. It reports work with governments in more than 45 countries and had about 1,000 staff in 2026. Its largest donor is Larry Ellison's foundation, which gave over £52 million in 2023, The Guardian reported.
cases.cite: Tony Blair Institute published programme descriptions; The Guardian, Apr 2025
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): Advisers placed openly at governments' request; nothing shows decisions served the institute or its donors.

cases.n: Universal Church bishop Crivella as senator, minister and Rio mayor
cases.rank: federal minister, senator and mayor of Rio de Janeiro
cases.d: Marcelo Crivella, a bishop of the Universal Church of the Kingdom of God (a Brazilian neo-Pentecostal church) and nephew of its founder Edir Macedo, held a run of public offices. He was a senator for Rio de Janeiro from 2003 to 2016, Minister of Fishing and Aquaculture under Dilma Rousseff in 2012–14, and mayor of Rio from 2017 to 2020. He was arrested on 22 December 2020, days before his term as mayor ended, in a corruption investigation.
cases.cite: The Guardian, 22 Dec 2020; Wikipedia biography
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): A bishop holding office; nothing shows the church steering his decisions, and his arrest is not tied to it.

cases.n: Evangelical pastor Damares Alves as minister, then senator
cases.rank: Minister of Women, Families and Human Rights; senator
cases.d: Damares Alves, an evangelical pastor who served in the Foursquare Gospel Church and the Lagoinha Baptist Church, was made Minister of Women, Families and Human Rights by President Jair Bolsonaro, serving from January 2019 to March 2022. She was then elected senator for the Federal District in 2022 for Republicanos, the party founded by pastors of the Universal Church, and took her seat in February 2023.
cases.cite: Wikipedia biography, citing Brazilian press
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): Only that the minister is an evangelical pastor; no decision shown steered by a church.

cases.n: Opus Dei numerary governed Kenya's central bank
cases.rank: Governor of the Central Bank of Kenya
cases.d: Patrick Njoroge, a numerary member of Opus Dei, governed the Central Bank of Kenya from June 2015 to June 2023. Opus Dei is a Catholic organisation whose celibate 'numerary' members live in its centres. Njoroge was nominated by President Uhuru Kenyatta and approved by Parliament in June 2015. As governor he also sat ex officio (by virtue of his post) on the IMF Board of Governors. His brother Anthony Muheria is Catholic archbishop of Nyeri.
cases.cite: Parliament of Kenya approval, 18 Jun 2015; Wikipedia biography and 'List of members of Opus Dei'
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): Only that the governor is an Opus Dei numerary; no decision shown steered by it.

cases.n: US Fellowship network's Uganda chair floated death-penalty gay bill
cases.rank: Minister of State for Trade, Industry and Cooperatives
cases.d: David Bahati, a Ugandan politician who chairs Uganda's National Prayer Breakfast Fellowship, first floated his 2009 Anti-Homosexuality Bill, which proposed the death penalty, at the 2008 Uganda prayer breakfast, journalist Jeff Sharlet reported. The Fellowship (also called The Family) is a US Christian network that runs national prayer breakfasts for politicians; Fellowship member Bob Hunter confirmed Bahati's link to the network to NPR. Bahati has been a state minister since 2021 and was re-appointed in 2026.
cases.cite: Jeff Sharlet reporting; NPR, Dec 2009; Wikipedia biography
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): The record shows a link to the Fellowship and the bill's launch at its event, not the network directing the bill.

cases.n: Ghanaian minister confirms Freemason membership at his vetting
cases.rank: Minister for Youth Development and Empowerment
cases.d: Freemasonry, a fraternal society whose members meet in lodges, has members in Ghana's government and parliament. George Opare Addo confirmed he is a Freemason, naming his lodge as 'Amity', at his parliamentary vetting as a minister on 22 January 2025, and was then confirmed as a minister in President Mahama's government. The question came from Minority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin, who had himself said in February 2024: 'I am a Freemason and a Catholic.'
cases.cite: Graphic Online (Ghana), Jan 2025
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): Only that the minister is a Freemason; no decision shown steered by a lodge.

cases.n: Ghana's security and transport ministers are serving Freemasons
cases.rank: Majority Leader; National Security and Transport ministers
cases.d: Freemasonry in Ghana counts serving ministers and the head of government business in parliament among its members. When the Grand Lodge of Ghana honoured the Asantehene (king of the Asante), Otumfuo Osei Tutu II, for 25 years in Freemasonry in May 2024, GhanaWeb reported that National Security Minister Albert Kan-Dapaah and Transport Minister Kweku Ofori Asiamah took part as members. It also reported that Majority Leader Alexander Afenyo-Markin had publicly said he is a Freemason. Former President John Kufuor has said he joined in 1967. The record shows membership and office; it does not show lodge direction of their decisions.
cases.cite: GhanaWeb, 26 May and 1 Jun 2024
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): Membership and office only, as the record itself says.

cases.n: Mourides placed in Senegal's government; presidents court their caliph
cases.d: Senegal's presidents have brought the Mourides, a Sufi Muslim brotherhood, close to government and court their caliph (spiritual leader). Abdoulaye Wade travelled to the Mouride holy city of Touba the day after his 2000 election and put Mourides in his government. Touba has run with wide autonomy from the state since 1928. President Bassirou Diomaye Faye visited Caliph Serigne Mountakha Mbacké on 7 August 2025 ahead of the Grand Magal pilgrimage, a pre-Magal visit that has become customary for heads of state.
cases.cite: Seneweb, Aug 2025; Wikipedia 'Mouride' citing academic sources
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): Presidents court the brotherhood and appointed members, but no decision is shown steered by it.

cases.n: Boutchichiya Sufi follower has run Morocco's religious ministry since 2002
cases.rank: Minister of Habous and Islamic Affairs
cases.d: Ahmed Toufiq, a follower of the Boutchichiya, Morocco's largest Sufi order, has been the king's Minister of Islamic Affairs, which oversees the country's mosques, since November 2002 under five prime ministers. Toufiq, a historian, has said a chance meeting with the order's sheikh, al-Abbas, set him on the Sufi path. In August 2025 a leaked letter from Toufiq warned the order about 'abuses' and 'appetites' during a dispute over its leadership.
cases.cite: Religion Unplugged, 13 Mar 2020; TelQuel, 26 Aug 2025 (headline)
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): Only that the minister follows the Sufi order; no decision shown steered by it.

cases.n: Nahdlatul Ulama's supreme leader became Indonesia's vice-president
cases.d: Ma'ruf Amin, supreme leader (rais 'aam) of Nahdlatul Ulama (NU), Indonesia's largest Muslim organisation, became the country's vice-president. NU is rooted in traditionalist and Sufi-influenced pesantren (Islamic boarding) schools. Amin was elected its supreme leader in 2015 and also chaired the Indonesian Ulema Council. President Joko Widodo picked him as running mate in August 2018; he resigned the NU post and served as vice-president from 2019 to 2024.
cases.cite: Wikipedia biography, citing Indonesian press
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): An NU leader became vice-president, but no decision is shown steered by NU.

cases.n: NAR figure Paula White heads the White House Faith Office
cases.rank: Senior Advisor, White House Faith Office
cases.d: Paula White, a televangelist whom Wikipedia's account of the New Apostolic Reformation (NAR) lists among its figures, holds a post inside the White House. The NAR is a network of self-styled apostles and prophets that seeks Christian influence over the 'seven mountains' of society, including government. On 7 February 2025 Trump, whose long-time spiritual adviser she is, created a White House Faith Office led by White. She had been a special adviser on faith in his first term.
cases.cite: White House announcement, Feb 2025; White House annual personnel report to Congress, 1 Jul 2025
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): Only that a figure listed among the NAR holds a White House post; no decision shown steered by the network.

cases.n: Opus Dei member Guillermo Lasso as president of Ecuador
cases.d: Guillermo Lasso, a banker reported by the newspaper El Universo since at least 2009 to be a supernumerary of Opus Dei, held Ecuador's presidency from May 2021 to November 2023. Opus Dei is a Catholic organisation of priests and lay members; supernumeraries are its married lay members, who follow its spiritual discipline while working in ordinary jobs.
cases.cite: El Universo, 2009; Wikipedia 'Guillermo Lasso' and 'List of members of Opus Dei'
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): Only that the president is reported to be an Opus Dei member; no decision shown steered by it.

cases.n: Opus Dei member Przemysław Wipler in Poland's Sejm
cases.d: Przemysław Wipler, reported by Gazeta Wyborcza as of 2023 to be a supernumerary (married lay member) of Opus Dei, the Catholic organisation of priests and lay members, holds a seat in Poland's parliament, the Sejm. He was elected for the Confederation party in October 2023 and in January 2024 became vice-chair of the parliamentary inquiry into the previous government's use of Pegasus spyware.
cases.cite: Gazeta Wyborcza, 2023; Sejm records; via Wikipedia
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): Only that the MP is reported to be an Opus Dei member; no decision shown steered by it.

cases.n: Opus Dei numerary Luis Silva as Chile's under-secretary of justice
cases.d: Luis Silva, a law professor and a numerary of Opus Dei, holds a senior post in Chile's justice ministry. Numeraries are celibate full members of Opus Dei, the Catholic organisation of priests and lay members, as La Tercera and El País reported when Silva topped the 2023 vote for Chile's Constitutional Council, the body elected to draft a new constitution, for the Republican Party. He took office as Undersecretary of Justice under President José Antonio Kast on 11 March 2026.
cases.cite: La Tercera, 8 May 2023; El País Chile, 12 May 2023; Government of Chile appointment, Mar 2026
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): Only that the under-secretary is an Opus Dei numerary; no decision shown steered by it.

cases.n: Party committee and state board seat inside TikTok owner ByteDance
cases.rank: party committee and state-held board seat in TikTok's parent
cases.d: The Chinese Communist Party and state have their own presence inside ByteDance, the Beijing company that owns TikTok and Douyin: it has had an internal party committee since 2014, and in 2021 a state-owned fund bought 1% of its main Chinese subsidiary and took a board seat. In December 2022 ByteDance admitted that employees had used TikTok data to track journalists who reported on the company, and fired four staff. The US Congress passed a 2024 law forcing TikTok's sale on national-security grounds, which the Supreme Court upheld in January 2025.
cases.cite: ByteDance admission Dec 2022; US Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act 2024; TikTok v. Garland (2025)
cases.who: China (Chinese Communist Party and state fund)
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): Party and state presence inside ByteDance, but the data misuse shown served the company itself; no decision shown made for the party.

cases.n: Revolutionary Guards-linked foundations bought Iran's telecom monopoly
cases.rank: controlling stake in the Telecommunication Company of Iran
cases.d: Foundations linked to Iran's Revolutionary Guards (the IRGC, Iran's ideological military force) gained control of the Telecommunication Company of Iran through an investor group. The company runs the country's fixed lines and owns the largest mobile operator, MCI. In 2009 the Mobin Trust Consortium, whose investors included those foundations, bought 50% plus one share for about US$7.8 billion in a privatisation, giving it control of the network the state uses to watch and filter communications. An IRGC unit announced in October 2018 that it had sold its share and left telecoms.
cases.cite: Iranian privatisation tender 2009; IRGC announcement Oct 2018
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): Control gained by buying the company in a privatisation, a takeover rather than a hidden placement.

cases.n: Chinese state-linked owner Wingtech and Dutch chipmaker Nexperia
cases.d: Through Wingtech, a Shanghai-listed firm in which almost 30% of shares trace back to the Chinese state, China gained a stake in the control of Nexperia, a Dutch chipmaker Wingtech bought in 2018 for US$3.6 billion. In October 2025 the Dutch economy ministry took control of Nexperia's governance under the Goods Availability Act, reportedly to stop chip know-how and production moving to China. China responded by banning exports of Nexperia chips packaged there, causing shortages for European carmakers. The Netherlands suspended its order in November 2025, and in February 2026 a Dutch court ordered an investigation into mismanagement at Nexperia.
cases.cite: Dutch Ministry of Economic Affairs order under the Goods Availability Act, Oct 2025; Dutch court order for a mismanagement inquiry, Feb 2026
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): An open purchase of the company; no hidden placement or decision for the Chinese state shown.

cases.n: FPL's consultants tied to dark money for Florida 'ghost' candidates
cases.d: Nonprofits partly overseen by the chief executive of Matrix LLC, a consulting firm then working for Florida Power & Light (FPL), the state's largest electric utility, channelled about $630,000 of the roughly $730,000 in dark money (political spending whose donors are hidden) that paid for 'ghost' candidates in the 2020 Florida Senate races. Republican operatives recruited these little-known candidates to split the vote and change who won seats; in District 37 the incumbent Democrat lost by under 40 votes. Several people were convicted or pleaded no contest and former senator Frank Artiles was charged; FPL was not charged, denies wrongdoing and says two outside law firms cleared it. Leaked Matrix records also showed surveillance of a journalist and payments to news outlets; FPL's chief executive retired in January 2023.
cases.cite: Florida criminal cases (Miami-Dade and Seminole); Floodlight / Mother Jones, 18 September 2024
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): Dark money for decoy election candidates from outside; FPL is not shown placing anyone inside or getting decisions made.

cases.n: Musk led DOGE while agencies it cut regulated his companies
cases.d: In 2025 Elon Musk, owner of Tesla, SpaceX and Neuralink, led the Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE), which cut staff and contracts across federal agencies, including some that regulated his companies. An April 2025 memo by Democratic staff of the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, under ranking member Richard Blumenthal, counted 65 active or potential federal enforcement actions against Musk's companies across 11 agencies and estimated that 40 of them carried $2.37 billion in potential liabilities that DOGE's influence could help them avoid. Musk denied conflicts and left DOGE in 2025.
cases.cite: US Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, Minority Staff Memorandum, 27 April 2025; The Register, 28 April 2025
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): The record gives estimates of what DOGE could help Musk's companies avoid, not a decision shown that served them.

cases.n: CDC director advised ex-Coca-Cola executive on lobbying the WHO
cases.rank: director, CDC Division for Heart Disease and Stroke Prevention
cases.d: Barbara Bowman, director of the Division for Heart Disease and Stroke Prevention at the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), advised Alex Malaspina, a former Coca-Cola senior vice-president and founder of the industry-funded International Life Sciences Institute, on how to approach the World Health Organization, which he said did not want to work with industry. The emails, from 2011 to 2015, were obtained under Freedom of Information requests and analysed in a study in The Milbank Quarterly in February 2019. Coca-Cola said the emails pre-dated its 2015 pledge to disclose research funding.
cases.cite: Hessari et al., The Milbank Quarterly 97(1), 2019; Mother Jones, 1 February 2019
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): A CDC official advising an ex-industry figure by email; no decision shown made for Coca-Cola.

cases.n: Big-bank lobby hired EU banking regulator's chief
cases.d: The Association for Financial Markets in Europe (AFME), the lobby group of Europe's largest banks, recruited the head of the European Banking Authority (EBA) while he still had access to the regulator's confidential information. The EBA writes and enforces common rules for EU banks. Adam Farkas, its executive director since 2011, left in February 2020 to run AFME. On 11 May 2020 European Ombudsman Emily O'Reilly found maladministration: the EBA should have forbidden the move, and should have cut off Farkas's access to confidential information as soon as he notified it of the new job. Moves like this, from regulator to the industry it regulates, are known as the 'revolving door'. The EBA then adopted a new revolving-door policy.
cases.cite: European Ombudsman decision, 11 May 2020; EUobserver, 12 May 2020
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): A regulator's chief left to work for the bank lobby; no decision at the regulator shown that served the banks.

cases.n: Shell and Unilever lobbied for Dutch tax cut in coalition talks
cases.rank: Prime Minister Mark Rutte's coalition talks
cases.d: Shell and Unilever got a tax cut they wanted into the programme of a new Dutch government during closed-door coalition talks. In October 2017 Mark Rutte's new government announced it would abolish the 15% Dutch dividend withholding tax, a tax on payouts to shareholders, although no party had campaigned for it. Memos released in April 2018, after pressure in Parliament, showed the two companies had lobbied for it during the 2017 coalition talks, and an August 2017 memo called the tax 'decisive' for Unilever's choice of headquarters. Rutte survived a censure vote. In October 2018, after Unilever dropped its move to Rotterdam, the government abandoned the plan.
cases.cite: Dutch government memos released to the House of Representatives, 24 April 2018; ESM Magazine (Reuters), 25 April 2018
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): Companies lobbying in coalition talks from outside; no company people placed inside government.

cases.n: Babiš kept control of Agrofert while serving as Czech PM
cases.d: Andrej Babiš, Czech prime minister, kept control of his own company Agrofert, a farming, food and chemicals group that receives EU farm subsidies, according to a European Commission audit. A 2017 Czech conflict-of-interest law led Babiš to put Agrofert into two trust funds, but the Commission audit published in 2021 concluded he still controlled the company and was in a conflict of interest, meaning he could influence public decisions on money going to his own business. He became prime minister again in December 2025. He took back sole ownership in October 2025 and on 20 February 2026 moved the shares to a new trust, saying the conflict was resolved.
cases.cite: European Commission audit, 2021; Radio Prague, 21 February 2026
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): The prime minister's own company and a conflict of interest; no outside party or decision shown that served it.

cases.n: Philip Morris's secret campaign to get inside WHO tobacco treaty
cases.rank: WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control (FCTC) meetings
cases.d: Philip Morris International (PMI), the tobacco company, ran a secret campaign to get into and weaken the WHO tobacco treaty, Reuters reported on 13 July 2017 from thousands of leaked company documents. The treaty, the FCTC, in force since 2005, commits governments to tax tobacco, ban advertising and keep the industry out of health policy (Article 5.3). The documents showed PMI lobbying delegates, trying to get into treaty meetings and fighting tax, advertising and warning-label rules from the Americas to Africa and Asia. A 2014 company presentation said 'Roadblocks are as important as solutions'. PMI said it had a right to take part in policy debates.
cases.cite: Reuters, 'Inside Philip Morris' campaign to subvert the global anti-smoking treaty', 13 July 2017
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): Lobbying delegates and trying to get into meetings from outside; no one inside shown working for PMI.

cases.n: Dan Gertler used friendship with Kabila for Congo mining deals
cases.rank: President Joseph Kabila; state miner Gécamines
cases.d: Dan Gertler, an Israeli mining and oil investor, used his long friendship with Congolese president Joseph Kabila to obtain mining and oil deals from the state, according to the US Treasury. In December 2017 the Treasury sanctioned him under the Global Magnitsky Act, a US law for punishing corruption and abuses abroad, saying he amassed a fortune through hundreds of millions of dollars of opaque and corrupt mining and oil deals in the DRC using that friendship. Under a later settlement with the Congolese state his Ventora group handed back mining and oil licences and agreed to pay royalties to the state miner Gécamines. Gertler denies wrongdoing.
cases.cite: US Treasury OFAC Global Magnitsky designation, 21 December 2017
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): Favours from a friendship with the president; no people, payments or control inside the state shown.

cases.n: Sanctioned state contractor Tagwirei made a Zimbabwe minister
cases.rank: Minister of Economic Development and Investment Promotion; ZANU-PF Central Committee
cases.d: Kudakwashe Tagwirei, a businessman whose company profited from state contracts, moved into Zimbabwe's ruling party and then its cabinet. His firm Sakunda Holdings grew through fuel trading with Trafigura and a $3 billion state 'Command Agriculture' contract from 2017 to 2019 paid with Treasury bills. In August 2020 the US Treasury sanctioned him, accusing him of misappropriating public funds and supporting senior officials; the UK followed in July 2021 and the US extended sanctions in March 2024. He was co-opted onto ZANU-PF's Central Committee in October 2025, and in October 2026 President Mnangagwa appointed him a cabinet minister. He denies the allegations.
cases.cite: US Treasury designation, 5 August 2020 and March 2024; UK sanctions, July 2021
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): A contractor took party and cabinet posts; no decision in office shown serving his firm.

cases.n: SQM secretly funded Chilean politicians through fake invoices
cases.rank: politicians and parties across Chile's spectrum
cases.d: SQM, a Chilean lithium and fertiliser miner whose main shareholder is Julio Ponce Lerou, former son-in-law of dictator Augusto Pinochet, secretly paid money to Chilean politicians' campaigns and parties. From 2015 Chilean prosecutors investigated how politicians, advisers and relatives issued fake invoices that SQM paid, passing money to campaigns in breach of finance laws. In 2017 SQM settled US Foreign Corrupt Practices Act charges under a deferred prosecution agreement, a deal in which charges are suspended if the company pays and reforms; the US Justice Department confirmed in 2020 that it had met the terms. In 2024 SQM agreed a long-term lithium partnership with the state copper company Codelco.
cases.cite: Chilean Public Prosecutor's Office (Penta-SQM case); US DOJ deferred prosecution agreement, January 2017
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): Secret campaign funding, but no decision by the politicians shown serving SQM.

cases.n: Kuciak's last story — 'Ndrangheta-linked man's partner in PM's office
cases.rank: chief state adviser in the Prime Minister's office
cases.d: Mária Trošková, a former business partner of Antonino Vadala, an Italian businessman named in investigations into the 'Ndrangheta (the Calabrian mafia), had become an assistant to Slovakia's Prime Minister Robert Fico. Journalist Ján Kuciak was working on this when he and his fiancée Martina Kušnírová were shot dead in February 2018. His unfinished article, published by OCCRP partners on 28 February 2018, described Vadala's farm companies in eastern Slovakia. Trošková and Security Council secretary Viliam Jasaň stepped aside in March 2018, and Fico resigned that month after mass protests. No court has found that the Prime Minister's office acted for the 'Ndrangheta.
cases.cite: OCCRP / Aktuality.sk, 'The Model, the Mafia, and the Murderers', 28 February 2018
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): Only a business link between a PM's aide and an 'Ndrangheta-linked man; no action for the mafia shown.

cases.n: Marty report: KLA-era 'Drenica Group' led by Kosovo's PM
cases.d: A Council of Europe report said a criminal group of former Kosovo Liberation Army (KLA) commanders, the 'Drenica Group', was led by Kosovo's own Prime Minister, Hashim Thaçi. In December 2010 Swiss senator Dick Marty told the Council's Parliamentary Assembly that the group controlled criminal trades including heroin, and he found 'credible, convergent indications' of organ trafficking from captives after the 1999 war. The Assembly endorsed the report on 25 January 2011; Thaçi denied it. An EU task force later reported compelling indications of war crimes, which led to the Kosovo Specialist Chambers, where Thaçi has been on trial for war crimes since 2023. The organised-crime claims have not been tested in court.
cases.cite: Council of Europe PACE report by Dick Marty, December 2010, adopted 25 January 2011
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): Crimes run by the prime minister's own circle; no outside party placed inside.

cases.n: Plahotniuc — oligarch who controlled Moldova jailed for bank theft
cases.rank: Democratic Party leader and first vice-president of Parliament
cases.d: Vlad Plahotniuc, a businessman who led the Democratic Party and was widely described as controlling Moldova's government and parliamentary majority, was sentenced on 22 April 2026 to 19 years over the 2014 theft of about $1 billion, equal to 12% of Moldova's GDP, from three banks. The money was drained through loans that were paid off with new loans and moved through UK and Hong Kong shell companies. Plahotniuc fled in 2019, was arrested in Greece in July 2025 and extradited on 25 September 2025. During parliamentary hearings, the deputy head of the security service said President Nicolae Timofti had known of the theft since 2013.
cases.cite: Chișinău court, sentence of 22 April 2026; Moldovan parliamentary hearings on the bank fraud
cases.who: Plahotniuc network and the 'theft of the billion' group
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): The record does not show how his control of the state served the bank theft.

cases.n: Bai crime family's head ran Myanmar's Kokang zone and sat as MP
cases.rank: first head of the Kokang Self-Administered Zone; Shan State MP
cases.d: Bai Suocheng, head of a family that ran scam and gambling centres in Laukkai, led the government of Myanmar's Kokang Self-Administered Zone as its first chief and sat as a Shan State MP for the army-backed USDP party. He was a former deputy commander of the Kokang armed group. Myanmar handed him to China in 2024. In November 2025 the Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court sentenced him, his son Bai Yingcang and three associates to death for telecom fraud and gambling run under armed guard, linked to the deaths of six Chinese citizens. Bai Suocheng died in custody; four Bai group members were executed on 2 February 2026, days after 11 members of the Ming family were executed.
cases.cite: Shenzhen Intermediate People's Court (November 2025); Guangdong High Court (24 December 2025); Caixin and SCMP
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): A crime family's head held office; no decision in office shown serving the family.

cases.n: Gangster Mukhtar Ansari held a UP assembly seat five times
cases.rank: Member of the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly (Mau)
cases.d: Mukhtar Ansari, a gang leader, won the Mau seat in the Uttar Pradesh state assembly five times between 1996 and 2022, twice for the Bahujan Samaj Party, much of that time from prison, where he was held from 2005. He faced 65 criminal cases and had been convicted in eight, including a murder case in 2023 and a life sentence in March 2024 in a fake arms licence case. He died in custody on 28 March 2024. His son Abbas Ansari won the seat in 2022.
cases.cite: Uttar Pradesh courts; The Indian Express, 29 March 2024
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): A gangster won a seat; no decision in office shown serving his gang.

cases.n: Bikie gang members held roles in CFMEU construction union
cases.d: Members of outlaw motorcycle gangs (bikies) and underworld figures held roles in the construction division of the CFMEU union on Victorian government building projects, media reports said in 2024. In August 2024 the federal government placed the division into administration under Mark Irving KC. An interim report by Geoffrey Watson SC in September 2024 found efforts to remove bikies inadequate and recommended further investigation of delegates' links to motorcycle gangs. In 2026 a further report's claims that Victorian ministers ignored warnings were referred to police, and Queensland held a commission of inquiry into the union.
cases.cite: Federal administration of the CFMEU construction division (August 2024); Geoffrey Watson SC interim report (September 2024); Queensland Commission of Inquiry into the CFMEU (2026)
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): Gang members held union roles; no decision shown serving the gangs, and a union is outside the test.

cases.n: Georges Pompidou: Rothschild general manager to French prime minister
cases.d: Georges Pompidou went from running Banque Rothschild, the French bank of the Rothschild banking family, to heading France's government. A literature teacher, he was hired in 1953 by Guy de Rothschild and was the bank's general manager from 1956 to 1962; Charles de Gaulle also hired him to run the Anne de Gaulle Foundation. De Gaulle made him Prime Minister in 1962, and he was elected President in 1969 and died in office in 1974. His move from the bank to the head of government is the best-known French case of a banker going straight to the top office. No court or inquiry has found that the bank directed his policies.
cases.cite: Wikipedia 'Georges Pompidou'
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): A banker took office; no decision shown serving the bank.

cases.n: Emmanuel Macron: Rothschild partner to Economy Minister and President
cases.rank: Élysée deputy secretary-general; Economy Minister; President
cases.d: Emmanuel Macron moved from the investment bank Rothschild & Cie Banque into the French posts that set economic and banking policy. He left the General Inspectorate of Finance, the state's financial audit body, in September 2008 for Rothschild, became a partner in 2010 and led Nestlé's €9 billion purchase of Pfizer's infant-nutrition unit; he reported earning about €2 million between December 2010 and May 2012. On 15 May 2012 he became deputy secretary-general of the Élysée (the president's office) under François Hollande, then Economy Minister (2014–16), and has been President since May 2017. Rival Benoît Hamon accused him of conflicts of interest from his Rothschild years, which Macron called 'demagogy'. No court or inquiry has found that the bank directs his policies.
cases.cite: Le Monde, 16 May 2012 ('un banquier d'affaires nommé secrétaire général adjoint de l'Elysée'); Wikipedia 'Emmanuel Macron'
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): A banker took office; no decision shown serving the bank.

cases.n: Paul Warburg: Kuhn, Loeb partner on the first Federal Reserve Board
cases.rank: Member (1914–18) and vice chairman (1916–18), Federal Reserve Board
cases.d: Paul Warburg, a partner of the New York investment bank Kuhn, Loeb & Co., helped design the US central bank and then sat on the board that runs it. German-born, from the Hamburg Warburg banking family, he was the leading public advocate of a US central bank, advised Senator Aldrich's National Monetary Commission and attended the secret 1910 Jekyll Island meeting that drafted the plan. President Woodrow Wilson appointed him to the first Federal Reserve Board in August 1914, and he was its vice chairman from 1916 to 1918, resigning his Wells Fargo directorship on appointment. He later presided over the Fed's Federal Advisory Council (1924–26) and sat on the founding board of the Council on Foreign Relations from 1921.
cases.cite: Wikipedia 'Paul Warburg'

arch.t: Council on Foreign Relations — Submergence of US Sovereignty (Insider Testimony)

cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): A banker took a Fed seat; no decision shown serving his bank.

cases.n: Thomas Lamont: Morgan partner on the US reparations team at Versailles
cases.rank: US Treasury representative, Paris Peace Conference
cases.d: Thomas W. Lamont, a partner of J.P. Morgan & Co., the bank that had been Britain's and France's main lender in the US during the First World War, was appointed with Norman Davis to represent the US Treasury at the 1919 Paris Peace Conference, working on how much Germany should pay in reparations. Lamont later sat on the committees that drew up the Dawes Plan (1924) and Young Plan (1929), which reset those payments. Historian Carroll Quigley writes that Lamont gave £2,000 to fund the history of the Peace Conference commissioned in 1919 by the Hotel Majestic meeting of British and US experts, the project from which Chatham House grew, and lists him in the loose American Round Table group.
cases.cite: Wikipedia 'Thomas W. Lamont'; Quigley, The Anglo-American Establishment, p. 183; Tragedy and Hope, p. 950
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): A Morgan partner held a post; no decision shown serving the bank.

cases.n: Quigley: Morgan bank's men held top US offices
cases.rank: Secretary of State, Treasury and diplomatic posts held by Morgan associates
cases.d: Men from the J.P. Morgan bank's circle held top US public offices, historian Carroll Quigley argued in Tragedy and Hope (1966), describing a 'system of influence which centered on the J. P. Morgan office at 23 Wall Street' and names men in it including Walter Burns, Clinton Dawkins, Edward Grenfell, Willard Straight, Thomas Lamont, Dwight Morrow, Nelson Perkins, Russell Leffingwell, Elihu Root, John W. Davis, John Foster Dulles and S. Parker Gilbert. Root was Secretary of War and of State, Davis Solicitor General and ambassador to London, Leffingwell Assistant Treasury Secretary, Gilbert Agent General for Reparations in Berlin, and Dulles Secretary of State. He says banking families such as Baring, Lazard, Warburg, Rothschild and Morgan were devoted to 'the secret use of financial influence in political life'; the description is his.
cases.cite: Quigley, Tragedy and Hope (Macmillan, 1966), pp. 51–53
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): Morgan associates held offices; no decision shown serving the bank.

cases.n: Quigley: Lazard's Robert Brand placed bank men in wartime Washington posts
cases.rank: First Secretary and Counsellor, British Embassy; Combined Production and Resources Board
cases.d: Historian Carroll Quigley writes that Robert Brand, a managing director of the London bank Lazard Brothers and a leader of the Round Table network (a group of British officials and financiers), moved men from the bank into Britain's wartime posts in Washington. Adam D. Marris, son of Sir William Marris of the network's founding circle, got his Lazard job through Brand in 1929, joined the British Embassy in Washington in 1940 as First Secretary and later Counsellor (to 1945), then ran the Emergency Economic Committee for Europe and returned to Lazard in February 1946, later succeeding Brand as managing director. Brand, still at Lazard until May 1944, put his nephew Thomas Henry Brand in his place at the bank and then brought him to Washington as chief executive on the British side of the Combined Production and Resources Board. Quigley says the network was 'monopolizing' the wartime embassy.
cases.cite: Quigley, The Anglo-American Establishment, pp. 60, 80–81, 304; Tragedy and Hope, pp. 950–951
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): Lazard men held wartime posts; no decision shown serving the bank.

cases.n: Max Warburg: Hamburg banker on the Reichsbank council and at Versailles
cases.rank: German peace delegation expert; Reichsbank council
cases.d: Max Warburg, head of the Hamburg bank M. M. Warburg & Co. from 1910 to 1938, moved between his bank and German state posts, including the governing council of the Reichsbank, Germany's central bank. He advised Kaiser Wilhelm II before the First World War. On 12 March 1919 Foreign Minister Count Brockdorff-Rantzau named him one of six chief delegates for the Versailles peace talks; he declined and served as an expert, and on his recommendation his partner Carl Melchior became principal delegate for economic and financial questions. He sat on the Reichsbank's general council from 1924 and on the supervisory board of IG Farben (1925–31). After the Nazis took power he had to leave the council because he was Jewish; the bank was 'Aryanised' in 1938 and he emigrated to the United States.
cases.cite: German Wikipedia 'Max Warburg'; Wikipedia 'Max Warburg', 'M. M. Warburg & Co.'
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): A banker held state posts; no decision shown serving his bank.

cases.n: Felix Rohatyn: Lazard partner ran New York City's rescue finances
cases.d: Felix Rohatyn, a partner of the investment bank Lazard Frères, was put in charge of New York City's finances when the city ran out of money in April 1975. Governor Hugh Carey advanced state funds on condition that the city hand management of its finances to the state, and appointed Rohatyn to a panel that proposed the Municipal Assistance Corporation (MAC), a state body that borrowed on the city's behalf. As MAC chairman and chief negotiator with unions and creditors, Rohatyn insisted on a wage freeze, mass layoffs, a subway fare rise and tuition at the City University. A state law turned city sales and stock-transfer taxes into state taxes to secure MAC bonds, and an Emergency Financial Control Board oversaw the city budget. MAC sold almost $10 billion of bonds before winding up in 2008. Rohatyn was later US ambassador to France (1997–2000).
cases.cite: Wikipedia 'Felix Rohatyn', 'Municipal Assistance Corporation'
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): A banker ran city finances; no decision shown serving Lazard.

cases.n: Gary Cohn: Goldman president to White House economic chief
cases.d: Gary Cohn moved from the top of Goldman Sachs to run economic policy in the White House. He joined Goldman in 1990, ran its fixed income, currency and commodities division and was president and co-chief operating officer from 2006. On 20 January 2017 he became director of President Donald Trump's National Economic Council, which coordinates economic policy and does not require Senate confirmation. In that post he led the administration's work on the Tax Cuts and Jobs Act of 2017, which cut the corporate tax rate. He left in 2018.
cases.cite: Wikipedia 'Gary Cohn'
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): A Goldman president took a post; a general tax cut is not a decision shown serving Goldman.

cases.n: Mario Draghi: Goldman vice chairman to Bank of Italy, ECB and premier
cases.rank: Governor, Bank of Italy; President, ECB; Prime Minister
cases.d: Mario Draghi moved between Italy's Treasury, Goldman Sachs and the posts that regulate Europe's banks. As director-general of the Italian Treasury (1991–2001) he drafted the law still governing Italian financial markets and led the 1990s privatisations of state companies. He was then vice chairman and managing director of Goldman Sachs International (2002–05), leading its European business with governments and large companies. He became Governor of the Bank of Italy (2006), President of the European Central Bank (2011–19), which sets monetary policy for the euro and from 2014 supervised the euro area's largest banks, and Prime Minister of Italy (2021–22). Goldman's 2001 Greek currency swaps (separate record) were arranged before he joined the firm.
cases.cite: Wikipedia 'Mario Draghi'
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): A Goldman banker took offices; no decision shown serving Goldman.

cases.n: Mario Monti: Goldman adviser named senator for life and premier
cases.d: Mario Monti, a former EU commissioner who had been an international adviser to Goldman Sachs and Coca-Cola, was appointed to head Italy's government without an election. He became president of the Trilateral Commission, a private forum of business and political leaders, in 2010 and was a leading member of the Bilderberg group, an annual private conference of the same kind. On 9 November 2011 President Giorgio Napolitano appointed him a senator for life and on 12 November, after Silvio Berlusconi resigned in the debt crisis, asked him to form a government. His unelected cabinet of technocrats (experts rather than party politicians) ran Italy until 2013 and passed austerity and pension measures.
cases.cite: Wikipedia 'Mario Monti'

arch.t: Trilateral Commission — 19/20 Carter Senior Appointments Were Members

cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): A Goldman adviser and forum member became premier; no decision shown serving them.

cases.n: Mark Carney: Goldman banker to two central banks and Canada's premiership
cases.rank: Governor, Bank of Canada and Bank of England; Prime Minister
cases.d: Mark Carney moved from Goldman Sachs into the posts that regulate banks in Canada, Britain and worldwide, and then to head Canada's government. After 13 years at Goldman he joined the Bank of Canada as a deputy governor in 2003. He was Governor of the Bank of Canada (2008–13), Governor of the Bank of England (2013–20) and chair of the Financial Stability Board (2011–18), the international body that coordinates rules for banks and markets among the G20 economies. In March 2025 he became leader of the Liberal Party and Prime Minister of Canada, and won a seat in Parliament (Nepean) in April 2025.
cases.cite: Wikipedia 'Mark Carney'
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): A Goldman banker took offices; no decision shown serving Goldman.

cases.n: Jörg Kukies: Goldman Germany co-head to finance ministry and chancellery
cases.rank: State Secretary for Finance; Chancellery State Secretary; Finance Minister
cases.d: Jörg Kukies moved from Goldman Sachs into the German government post that oversees financial markets, and later became Finance Minister. He spent 17 years at Goldman, rising to co-head for Germany and Austria. Finance Minister Olaf Scholz made him state secretary for financial markets, the senior civil-service post in charge of banking and market policy, in 2018. From 2021 to 2024 he was state secretary in the Chancellery and Scholz's sherpa (personal negotiator) for G7 and G20 summits, and he was Finance Minister from November 2024 to May 2025.
cases.cite: Wikipedia 'Jörg Kukies'
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): A Goldman banker took offices; no decision shown serving Goldman.

cases.n: BlackRock runs the Fed's 2020 bond-buying; its executive joins White House
cases.rank: Federal Reserve emergency facilities; National Economic Council
cases.d: BlackRock, the world's largest asset manager, was hired by the US government to run public rescue programmes, and one of its executives moved into the White House post that coordinates economic policy. The Treasury retained BlackRock in 2009 for crisis work. In March 2020 the Federal Reserve chose it to manage its corporate bond-buying programmes, the $500 billion Primary Market Corporate Credit Facility and the Secondary Market Corporate Credit Facility, plus purchases of commercial mortgage securities. In 2021 Brian Deese, BlackRock's former global head of sustainable investing, became director of President Biden's National Economic Council.
cases.cite: Wikipedia 'BlackRock' (citing Pensions & Investments, 25 Mar 2020; Washington Post; CNBC, 20 Mar 2021)
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): An open public contract plus a former executive's post; no decision shown serving BlackRock.

cases.n: Friedrich Merz: BlackRock Germany chairman to Chancellor
cases.d: Friedrich Merz moved from chairing the German arm of BlackRock, the world's largest asset manager, back into politics and became head of Germany's government. He left the Bundestag (Germany's parliament) in 2009 after losing a power struggle with Angela Merkel and worked as a corporate lawyer at Mayer Brown. From 2016 to 2020 he chaired the supervisory board of BlackRock's German arm, a hire the Wall Street Journal headlined 'BlackRock Hires Former Merkel Deputy'. He returned to parliament in 2021, became leader of the CDU party and was elected Chancellor in May 2025.
cases.cite: Wikipedia 'Friedrich Merz' (citing Wall Street Journal, 17 Jan 2016)
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): A former BlackRock chairman became chancellor; no decision shown serving BlackRock.

cases.n: Citigroup executive's list mapped Obama's cabinet before the election
cases.d: Michael Froman, a Citigroup executive, sent Barack Obama's team a list of names for the new cabinet a month before the 2008 election, and most of them got the jobs. On 6 October 2008 Froman, who had followed Robert Rubin from the Treasury to Citi, emailed John Podesta, co-chair of Obama's transition team, from his Citigroup address with candidate lists, including an outline of 31 cabinet-level posts. The email became public when WikiLeaks published Podesta's emails in 2016. The New Republic found the list 'almost entirely on the money': Eric Holder, Janet Napolitano, Robert Gates, Rahm Emanuel, Peter Orszag, Arne Duncan, Eric Shinseki and Kathleen Sebelius all got the posts listed, and for Treasury it named Rubin, Larry Summers or Timothy Geithner. Froman joined the White House in 2009 and became US Trade Representative in 2013.
cases.cite: David Dayen, The New Republic, 14 Oct 2016 (WikiLeaks Podesta emails); Wikipedia 'Michael Froman'
cases.drop_reason: Not directly infiltration (Nov 2026 stricter test): A suggested cabinet list; no decision shown serving Citigroup.

cases.n: Banco Rural cash paid Brazilian deputies for their votes
cases.rank: Federal deputies of the governing coalition
