orgs.d: The Carlyle Group, a Washington private equity firm, supplied the Federal Reserve's first Vice Chair for Supervision. Randal Quarles, a Carlyle managing director on financial-services deals and founder of the Cynosure Group, held the post from 2017 to 2021. Under him, banks moved into the strictest oversight group only once their assets consistently averaged more than $100 billion, instead of $50 billion; the New York Times reported this delayed Silicon Valley Bank's move into tighter supervision before it collapsed in 2023.

orgs.d: ICICI Bank, one of India's largest private banks, supplied the head of the country's stock-market regulator. In 2024 Hindenburg Research alleged that she and her husband held stakes in offshore funds tied to the Adani Group, which SEBI was investigating, and the Congress party alleged she kept receiving ICICI benefits. Alex Azar, president of its largest division, Lilly USA, from 2012 to 2017, was confirmed to the post in January 2018. During his time at Lilly the price of its top-selling insulin roughly tripled, and Lilly was one of three companies sued over insulin pricing. Senator Ron Wyden said Azar had 'never, not one time, signed off on a decrease in the price of a drug.'

Sri Lankan police examined the payments in 2015–16, and a minister called for an inquiry in 2018 after the New York Times reported them. CHEC denied it. Unable to service its debts, Sri Lanka leased Hambantota for 99 years to a Chinese state firm in 2017.

Given a gold-export monopoly in 1990, it was paid compensation about 35 percent above its foreign earnings, with finance minister George Saitoti authorising an extra 15 percent over Treasury advisers' objections. Central Bank clerk David Munyakei exposed it in 1993 and was fired. The cost was put at over 10 percent of Kenya's GDP; the 2006 Bosire Commission traced KSh 158.3 billion in linked transactions.

Interior Minister John Reimberg said his money let Los Lobos keep local communities terrorised, and police said explosives used in local attacks were traced to a company he owns. A Haaretz investigation in 2021 found its main donors were the American billionaires Arthur Dantchik and Jeff Yass, with Dantchik's money perhaps 93% of its budget. The Commission's February 2025 'Omnibus I' rewrite and the Council's June position contained three of them. The final text, adopted in December 2025 and February 2026, removed the climate-plan duty and EU-wide civil liability, as Exxon had asked.

Days later the SEC dropped its lawsuit against Binance, and Trump pardoned Zhao in October 2025. Zhao's lawyer denied any pay-to-play arrangement.

channels.n: Condor founding: Santiago → Buenos Aires → Montevideo → Asunción → La Paz
channels.d: Chile's DINA convened intelligence chiefs in Santiago on 25 November 1975; Chile, Argentina, Uruguay, Paraguay and Bolivia signed the founding document in January 1976. Members shared intelligence and carried out cross-border kidnappings, torture and killings; Automotores Orletti in Buenos Aires was a key detention site.
channels.cite: US National Security Archive 2025 briefing book

channels.n: Condor expansion: Santiago → Brasília → Lima → Quito
channels.d: Brazil became a formal member in 1976; Peru and Ecuador joined in 1977–78. In 1980 Peruvian and Argentine agents kidnapped four Montonero militants in Lima, one of the last recorded Condor operations.
channels.cite: US National Security Archive 2025 briefing book

channels.n: Condor phase three: Santiago → Washington (Letelier, 1976)
channels.d: Former Chilean ambassador Orlando Letelier and Ronni Moffitt were killed by a car bomb in Washington in September 1976; an FBI report suggested it may have been a Condor 'phase three' mission. The Letelier case led to the 1979 public revelation of Condor.
channels.cite: US National Security Archive 2025 briefing book

channels.n: Condor: La Paz exile killed in Buenos Aires (1976)
channels.d: Former Bolivian president Juan José Torres was assassinated in Buenos Aires in 1976, a case listed among Condor's cross-border killings.

channels.n: Safari Club: Riyadh money, Paris airlift, Rabat & Cairo troops → Shaba (Zaire, 1977)
channels.d: Saudi Arabia paid, France supplied technology and Egypt and Morocco provided troops. In 1977 French aircraft flew Moroccan and Egyptian troops into Zaire's Shaba province to repel an invasion.

channels.n: Safari Club arms: Cairo → Mogadishu (Ogaden war)
channels.d: The club supplied arms to Somalia in exchange for Siad Barre distancing himself from the Soviet Union during the Ogaden war. BCCI reportedly helped finance and launder money for the club's operations.

channels.n: Aginter Press: Lisbon → Milan / Rome (explosives training)
channels.d: Judge Guido Salvini found Aginter instructors trained members of the Italian neo-fascist Avanguardia Nazionale in explosives, and linked the agency to the groups behind the December 1969 Piazza Fontana bombing in Milan.

channels.n: Aginter Press: Lisbon → Luanda / Lourenço Marques (colonial wars)
channels.d: Aginter allegedly worked against independence movements in Portugal's colonies of Angola, Mozambique and East Timor; disputed sources tie it to the killings of Amílcar Cabral and Eduardo Mondlane.

channels.n: Aginter Press flight: Lisbon → Alicante / Caracas (1974)
channels.d: After the April 1974 Carnation Revolution, members fled to a site near Alicante associated with the Paladin Group, and the agency reportedly escaped to Caracas.

channels.n: TFP spread: São Paulo → Buenos Aires / Santiago / Montevideo (1967) → Warsaw
channels.d: From the Brazilian TFP (1960), national TFPs were founded in Argentina, Chile and Uruguay in 1967 and in Poland in 1995; Poland's Ordo Iuris was founded in 2013 by the TFP-linked Christian Culture Association.

channels.n: NXIVM: Albany → Mexico City / Vancouver
channels.d: NXIVM ran centres in Mexico and Canada as well as the US; Emiliano Salinas, son of former president Carlos Salinas, and Ana Cristina Fox, daughter of Vicente Fox, have been accused of involvement, and the Vancouver chapter recruited actresses including Allison Mack.

channels.n: Kingdom of Jesus Christ: Davao → California / Hawaii
channels.d: A US grand jury indicted Quiboloy in 2021 for child sex trafficking and misuse of church donations; FBI raids hit church sites in California, Texas and Hawaii.

channels.n: Saudi trust account through the US Treasury
channels.d: Saudi money deposited in a US Treasury trust account paid for US technical staff placed in Saudi agencies under the 1974 Joint Commission.

channels.n: NED grants to Venezuela's Cedice
channels.d: From 1998 NED's business institute CIPE made regular grants to Cedice, Atlas's Caracas think tank, whose director signed the 2002 Carmona Decree.

channels.n: Pilgrims Society: London ↔ New York, 1902–03
channels.d: The London society (1902) and New York society (1903) hold reciprocal membership and welcome each other's ambassadors.

channels.n: Fuzhou and Qingtian police bureaus to European 'service stations'
channels.d: Safeguard Defenders listed stations run for the Fuzhou city police in Dublin, Prato, Budapest, Paris, Prague and Athens, among others.

channels.n: Qingtian county police to stations in Rome, Milan, Florence, Vienna, Frankfurt
channels.d: Stations listed for the Qingtian County Public Security Bureau, a home county of many Chinese migrants in Italy and Austria.

channels.n: Moscow to Paris — Front National bank loan
channels.d: €9 million loan from the First Czech Russian Bank to the Front National, 2014.

channels.n: Ankara Diyanet to DITIB Cologne
channels.d: DITIB's imams are trained in Ankara and paid as Turkish civil servants by the Diyanet.

channels.n: Erik Prince's security deals with governments, 2019–2026
channels.d: A UN panel found Prince broke the Libya arms embargo in 2019; in 2025–26 he made security deals with Ecuador's president, ran anti-gang operations in Haiti through Vectus Global, and sent men and drones to help Congo's army at Uvira.
channels.cite: UN Panel of Experts on Libya, Feb 2021; Reuters 2025–26

channels.n: Diyanet imam network in Western Europe
channels.d: Turkey's Diyanet sends state-employed imams to mosques run by its branches abroad. Germany investigated DITIB imams for spying (2017), Austria reviewed the permits of about 40 ATIB imams (2018), a Dutch parliamentary inquiry found strong Diyanet political influence (2020), and Belgian State Security found a Diyanet employee in the new Brussels mosque body (2020).
channels.cite: Politico Europe 2017; Al Jazeera 2018; DutchNews 2020; Belgian Justice Ministry 2020

channels.n: Gulf Salafi funding to Belgian and Dutch mosques
channels.d: The Muslim World League ran the Great Mosque of Brussels for Saudi Arabia until Belgium ended the lease in 2018; the 2020 Dutch parliamentary inquiry traced Salafi mosque funding to donors in Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, the UAE and Qatar.

channels.n: Moscow Patriarchate churches cut off by neighbouring states
channels.d: After the 2022 invasion, Latvia (2022), Estonia (2024) and Ukraine (2024) used laws, residence permits and bans to sever local Orthodox churches from the Moscow Patriarchate.
channels.cite: Wikipedia articles on the Latvian, Estonian and Ukrainian churches; ERR News

channels.n: Basel: central bank governors' meetings
channels.d: Governors of the main central banks have met privately in Basel since 1930, monthly in the 1930s and every two months since 1998; Quigley described this as the apex of a world system of financial control.
channels.cite: Wikipedia 'Bank for International Settlements'; Quigley, Tragedy and Hope p. 324

channels.n: NSA access to Danish cables used to spy on European leaders (2012–14)
channels.d: Per the Danish FE's 'Dunhammer' review, the NSA used Danish cable intercepts to wiretap German leaders, with reported targets in Sweden, Norway and France.

channels.n: UAE money to Alp Services to target Europeans (2017–21)
channels.d: At least €5.7m paid via an Emirati front to Alp, which compiled files on people in 18 European countries, with the largest counts in Belgium, Italy and Norway.

channels.n: Calvi's flight: Milan → London (Blackfriars Bridge, 1982)
channels.d: Roberto Calvi, Ambrosiano chairman and P2 member, fled Italy on a false passport as the bank failed. He was found hanging from Blackfriars Bridge on 18 June 1982; Italian authorities reopened it as murder and prosecuted Licio Gelli and Giuseppe Calò.
channels.drop_reason: An escape route after the bank failed; the P2 and Ambrosiano infiltration is already carried by channels 0 and 1.

channels.n: P2 lodges in South America: Rome → Montevideo / São Paulo / Caracas
channels.d: P2 had lodges in Uruguay, Brazil and Venezuela as well as Argentina and Chile. Gelli took refuge in Uruguay in 1981 after his list was found.
channels.drop_reason: Shows only that P2 had lodges in other countries and that Gelli hid in Uruguay; no office-holders or institutions are shown.

channels.n: Gelli's escape: Arezzo → Geneva (1982–88)
channels.d: Gelli was arrested in Geneva in 1982 while trying to withdraw money, escaped prison in 1983, surrendered in 1987 and was extradited to Italy in 1988.
channels.drop_reason: A fugitive's arrest and escape route, not a route of infiltration.

channels.n: WACL / Taiwan covert aid: Taipei → Tegucigalpa (Contras)
channels.d: After the 1987 Iran-Contra revelations, reports showed Taiwanese covert military aid to the Contras, who were based in Honduras; League chairman Ku Cheng-kang reportedly helped arrange it and Taiwan's Foreign Ministry confirmed the activity.
channels.drop_reason: Covert military aid to rebel forces; no one is shown placed inside a government or institution.

channels.n: CAUSA: New York → Contras in Honduras / Nicaragua
channels.d: CAUSA International, founded by the Unification movement in New York in 1980 and active in 21 Latin American countries, aided the Nicaraguan Contras.
channels.drop_reason: Aid to the Contra rebels; no one is shown inside a government or institution.

channels.n: Gülen movement base: İzmir → Saylorsburg, Pennsylvania (1999)
channels.d: The movement began in İzmir, where Gülen set up student boarding houses from 1966; it moved its base to Pennsylvania in 1999, where Gülen lived until his death in October 2024.
channels.drop_reason: The movement moving its own base; nothing about getting inside an institution.

channels.n: School seizures: Ankara → Bishkek (Sapat schools to Maarif)
channels.d: After 2016 Turkey pressed governments to close or hand over Gülen-linked schools. Kyrgyzstan transferred management of the Gülen-linked Sapat schools to Turkey; Turkey's Maarif Foundation said in 2021 it had taken over 216 schools in 44 countries.
channels.cite: Stockholm Center for Freedom; Turkish Minute (2021)
channels.drop_reason: Turkey openly pressing governments to hand over schools; a state-to-state transfer, not infiltration.

channels.n: Brotherhood branches → Hamas: Cairo / Amman → Gaza
channels.d: Hamas began in 1987 as a Brotherhood offshoot. On 13 January 2026 the US Treasury designated the Egyptian and Jordanian branches as Specially Designated Global Terrorists for support to Hamas.
channels.cite: US Treasury designation 13 Jan 2026 (Times of Israel)
channels.drop_reason: A US terrorism designation of two branches; designation and offshoot history are not infiltration.

channels.n: Le Cercle: Paris → Bonn (founding axis)
channels.d: Antoine Pinay and Jean Violet founded the circle in 1952–53 with Konrad Adenauer and Franz Josef Strauss; Franco-German reconciliation was an early aim.
channels.drop_reason: Le Cercle's founding axis between its founders; the record shows a forum being set up, not anyone placed inside an institution.

channels.n: Le Cercle: Paris / London → Pretoria (apartheid delegation)
channels.d: South Africa sent the only official government delegation to the circle; in the 1970s–80s it was tied to the apartheid state and backed Renamo and UNITA.
channels.drop_reason: A government sending a delegation to a private forum and the forum backing rebels; no one is shown inside an institution.

channels.n: Bilderberg → Val-Duchesse dinner: Oosterbeek → Brussels (2009)
channels.d: In November 2009, outside its annual conference, Bilderberg held a dinner at the Château of Val-Duchesse in Brussels to promote Herman Van Rompuy's candidacy for President of the European Council.
channels.drop_reason: Bilderberg is a venue for private meetings and Oosterbeek its first meeting place; the dinner promoting a candidate names no infiltrator who placed people or money inside the EU.

channels.n: Aum Shinrikyo: Tokyo → Moscow → Podgorica
channels.d: Aum built a Russian following; a 2000 plot to free Asahara involved a Russian member. Russia opened a criminal case and banned the group in 2016, the same year Montenegro expelled 58 foreigners linked to it.
channels.drop_reason: Aum's foreign following, a plot and later bans; none of this is someone inside an institution.

channels.n: El Yunque: Puebla → Madrid (HazteOír)
channels.d: Álvaro Delgado linked El Yunque to Spain's HazteOír and CitizenGo; in 2014 a Madrid judge said evidence possibly showed links between HazteOír members and El Yunque but could not confirm the organisation exists.
channels.drop_reason: An alleged link between El Yunque and a Spanish NGO that a court could not confirm; no institution is shown being entered.

channels.n: Sangh overseas: Nagpur → Nairobi (1947) → London
channels.d: The RSS's overseas wing began in Nairobi on 14 January 1947 as the Bharatiya Swayamsevak Sangh, later the Hindu Swayamsevak Sangh, with branches in Kenya, the UK, Australia and Nepal.
channels.drop_reason: The RSS's overseas branches existing; no office-holders abroad are shown.

channels.n: Gulen-linked teachers removed or targeted for removal to Turkey, 2017–2021
channels.d: Malaysia deported three Turks to Turkey on 11 May 2017; an attempt to fly Veysel Akcay out of Ulaanbaatar was stopped on 27 July 2018 when Mongolian authorities grounded the plane; Orhan Inandi was taken from Bishkek to Turkey in mid-2021, which Erdogan announced on 5 July 2021.
channels.cite: Al Jazeera 12 May 2017; Euronews 28 July 2018; 24.kg 17 August 2021
channels.drop_reason: Deportations and renditions of teachers by host states, with no one shown inside those states' institutions working for Turkey.

channels.n: Gulen schools handed to Turkey's Maarif Foundation — Pakistan
channels.d: Pakistan's Supreme Court ordered on 28 December 2018 that Pak-Turk schools be transferred to the Turkiye Maarif Foundation.
channels.drop_reason: A Pakistani court ordering schools transferred to a Turkish foundation; an open legal transfer, not infiltration.

channels.n: Red Notice requests from member governments to Lyon
channels.d: Governments file notices with the General Secretariat in Lyon; notices later found political were refused or deleted, sometimes after arrests abroad.
channels.drop_reason: Governments filing Red Notice requests through Interpol's normal channel; using a system is not getting inside it.

channels.n: Round Table groups: London → dominion capitals, 1909–1915
channels.d: Lionel Curtis toured the dominions in 1910–11 setting up local Round Table groups (Canada, South Africa, Australia, New Zealand; Newfoundland 1912). Quigley adds India and a loose US group by 1915. City placement for each dominion group is approximate.
channels.cite: Wikipedia 'Round Table movement'; Quigley, Tragedy and Hope, p. 950
channels.drop_reason: Lionel Curtis setting up local discussion groups; no office-holders or institutions are shown.

channels.n: Chatham House → dominion institutes of international affairs, 1927 onward
channels.d: Quigley writes that Chatham House set up branch institutes in each dominion, each formed around the local Round Table members, the earliest in Canada and Australia in 1927, with the question taken up at the 1933 Toronto Commonwealth relations conference. Dates for each institute are not verified here.
channels.cite: Quigley, The Anglo-American Establishment, ch. 10, p. 191
channels.drop_reason: Founding of branch institutes abroad with unverified dates; nothing shows anyone placed in an institution.

channels.n: Morgan–Lazard axis: New York ↔ London
channels.d: Quigley describes the 'chief backbone' of the network as financial cooperation between the Morgan bank in New York and London financiers led by Lazard Brothers and Morgan, Grenfell; he says Milner refused a Morgan partnership in London in 1901 and that Brand and then Adam Marris were managing directors of Lazard. This is Quigley's account.
channels.drop_reason: Business cooperation between banks, per Quigley; no one is shown inside a government or institution.

channels.n: Institute of Pacific Relations conference circuit, 1925–1936
channels.d: IPR conferences met at Honolulu (1925, 1927), Kyoto (1929), Shanghai (1931), Banff (1933) and Yosemite (1936). Quigley says the British and dominion delegations were drawn from the same Milner Group circles as the Commonwealth relations conferences.
channels.cite: Quigley, The Anglo-American Establishment, ch. 10; Wikipedia 'Institute of Pacific Relations'
channels.drop_reason: The line joins conference venues only; a conference circuit is where people met, and no infiltration route is shown.

channels.n: UAE–Amdjarass–Darfur supply route to the RSF (UN panel)
channels.d: A UN Panel of Experts report leaked in January 2024 found 'credible' evidence that the UAE flew weapons to Sudan's Rapid Support Forces several times a week through the airstrip at Amdjarass in northern Chad, from where supplies crossed into Darfur. The UAE says its 122 flights carried humanitarian aid.
channels.cite: UN Panel of Experts on Sudan (Jan 2024), reported by Al Jazeera
channels.drop_reason: An arms supply route to an armed group; no one is shown inside an institution.

channels.n: Russian military air bridge Syria–eastern Libya for Wagner
channels.d: UN monitors and US Africa Command reported Russian military flights from Syria to eastern Libya supplying Wagner and Haftar's forces in 2019–20, including 338 flights counted in one UN report and Syrian fighters recruited by Wagner flown in on at least 33 Cham Wings flights. Russia later used eastern Libyan bases as logistics hubs for Africa Corps.
channels.cite: UN Panel of Experts on Libya; AFRICOM, as summarised on Wikipedia
channels.drop_reason: A military supply route for Wagner; logistics, not infiltration.

channels.n: Chinese police outposts in the Americas
channels.d: Outposts that Safeguard Defenders attributed to the Fuzhou city and Qingtian county police. The Manhattan site led to US convictions (2024, 2026); the RCMP closed its Quebec probe in 2025 without charges; no Latin American government has reported findings.
channels.cite: Safeguard Defenders reports, 2022; Wikipedia 'Chinese police overseas service stations'
channels.drop_reason: Overseas police outposts aimed at diaspora; the record shows no one inside host-country institutions working for them.

channels.n: Indian intelligence plots against Sikh activists in North America
channels.d: Canada linked agents of India's government to the killing of Hardeep Singh Nijjar and expelled six diplomats; US prosecutors charged RAW officer Vikash Yadav with directing a plot to kill Gurpatwant Singh Pannun in New York and said he sent video of Nijjar's body to the go-between.
channels.cite: Government of Canada, October 2024; US v. Yadav and Gupta (S.D.N.Y.)
channels.drop_reason: Assassination plots against activists; no one is shown inside a host-country institution.

channels.n: Russian Interior Ministry police training in Central America
channels.d: Russia's Interior Ministry runs a police training centre in Managua for Nicaraguan and regional officers; the US Treasury sanctioned it on 15 May 2024.
channels.drop_reason: An openly established police training centre; an open state-to-state arrangement.

channels.n: China's Ministry of Public Security police cooperation in the Pacific
channels.d: China's Ministry of Public Security has embedded officers in Fiji's police (2013–2024), sent advisory teams to the Solomon Islands (from 2022), Kiribati and Vanuatu (from 2023), and supplied equipment and training in China.
channels.cite: East Asia Forum, 7 March 2024; RFA/BenarNews, 20 March 2024
channels.drop_reason: Police cooperation under open agreements; the record shows no hidden role beyond what was agreed.

channels.n: Prince Group assets seized across Asia and London
channels.d: After the US and UK acted against Chen Zhi on 14 October 2025, the UK froze 19 London properties, Singapore seized S$150 million, Taiwan seized NT$4.5 billion and Hong Kong HK$2.75 billion.
channels.cite: US DOJ / UK sanctions, October 2025, as summarised on Wikipedia
channels.drop_reason: Asset seizures after sanctions; the infiltration (Chen Zhi as Hun Sen's adviser) is in Phnom Penh, not along this line.

channels.n: Unification Church honours and fees to heads of government
channels.d: From its Seoul headquarters the Unification Church, through the Universal Peace Federation and the Sunhak Peace Prize, gave a governance award to Cambodia's sitting prime minister (2019), a US$1 million-class peace prize to Senegal's sitting president (2020) and speaking fees of $2–2.5 million to Donald Trump (2021–22).
channels.drop_reason: Publicly awarded prizes and speaking fees; the record shows no decision bought or hidden payment.

channels.n: US Christian lobbies and Uganda's anti-gay laws
channels.d: Journalist Jeff Sharlet reported that David Bahati, chair of Uganda's Fellowship-linked National Prayer Breakfast, floated his 2009 bill at the 2008 breakfast; an activist named Family Watch International's president as a lobbyist for the 2023 Act.
channels.drop_reason: Repeats the Bahati story in channel 36; the rest is outside lobbying by Family Watch International, not someone inside an institution.

channels.n: Kokang scam bosses handed from Laukkai to Chinese courts
channels.d: Myanmar handed Kokang family leaders to China in 2023–24; the Bai group was tried in Shenzhen and the Ming family in Wenzhou, and members of both were executed in early 2026.
channels.drop_reason: A handover of crime bosses to Chinese courts; prosecution, not a route of infiltration.

channels.n: Rothschild five-house network
channels.d: Mayer Amschel Rothschild's five sons set up cooperating houses in Frankfurt, London, Paris, Vienna and Naples, which moved government money across Europe, including British war subsidies before 1815.
channels.cite: Quigley, Tragedy and Hope p. 51; Wikipedia 'Rothschild family'
channels.drop_reason: The family's own branch network moving government money openly; no one is placed inside a government.

channels.n: Morgan axis: 23 Wall Street–Morgan, Grenfell–Morgan, Harjes
channels.d: J.P. Morgan & Co. worked with its London affiliate (J.S. Morgan & Co., later Morgan, Grenfell) and Paris affiliate (Morgan, Harjes); in 1914–17 this axis handled British and French war purchasing and loans in the US. Quigley calls the New York–London tie to Lazard Brothers 'the chief backbone' of the Round Table organisation.
channels.cite: Wikipedia 'J. P. Morgan', 'American entry into World War I'; Quigley, Tragedy and Hope p. 951
channels.drop_reason: A bank's own branch network and its open role as British and French purchasing agent; no one is placed inside a government along this line.

channels.n: Schiff's Japanese war loans
channels.d: Jacob Schiff met Bank of Japan deputy governor Takahashi Korekiyo in Paris in April 1904 and floated about $200 million of Japanese war bonds in New York.
channels.drop_reason: An open bond issue for Japan arranged at a meeting in Paris; lending, not infiltration.

channels.n: Scientology members inside Ontario police and law offices: Saint Hill → Toronto
channels.d: Operation Snow White, run by the Church of Scientology's Guardian's Office from Saint Hill Manor in England, extended to Canada. The Church of Scientology of Toronto placed members as staff inside the Ontario Provincial Police and the Ontario Ministry of the Attorney General, which runs prosecutions in the province, and also targeted the Royal Canadian Mounted Police. On 25 June 1992 the church itself was convicted of breach of the public trust, a crime of abusing a public position; seven members were convicted in all and the church was fined $250,000. The Court of Appeal for Ontario later rejected its appeal.
channels.cite: R. v. Church of Scientology of Toronto (1992); Court of Appeal for Ontario, 1997
channels.drop_reason: A local branch operation in Toronto; no documented channel from England.

channels.n: Mont Pelerin Society members in top economic posts
channels.d: The Mont Pelerin Society, a free-market society of economists and thinkers that works to spread free-market ideas into policy, has had members in the top economic posts of several governments. Friedrich Hayek founded it in 1947 at a meeting in the Swiss village of Mont Pèlerin; it is now headquartered at Texas Tech University in Lubbock, Texas. Members who held office include Ludwig Erhard, who joined in 1950 while West Germany's economics minister and used its meetings to test his plans, Luigi Einaudi (President of Italy), Václav Klaus (Czech finance minister, prime minister and president), Carlos Cáceres (Chilean finance minister) and Ranil Wickremesinghe (Sri Lankan prime minister). No inquiry has found that the society directed their decisions.
channels.cite: Wikipedia 'Mont Pelerin Society'; Wikipedia 'Mont Pelerin Society' (headquarters at Texas Tech University); Mont Pelerin Society Directory (2010)
channels.drop_reason: A membership network, not a channel from one place; the points spanned decades.

channels.n: Susurluk crash exposed Grey Wolves working with the state: Ankara → Susurluk
channels.d: The Grey Wolves, the militant youth wing of Turkey's Nationalist Movement Party, worked alongside Turkish police and politicians, and a car crash near Susurluk on 3 November 1996 showed it. In the car were Abdullah Çatlı, the group's second-in-command, wanted by Interpol for murder and drug trafficking, who carried a false passport and a gun licence signed by Interior Minister Mehmet Ağar; Hüseyin Kocadağ, deputy chief of the Istanbul police; and MP Sedat Bucak. Ağar resigned within days. A parliamentary inquiry reported in April 1997 that state bodies had used the Grey Wolves, and in 2001 a court sentenced Ibrahim Şahin and Korkut Eken to six years each.
channels.cite: Wikipedia 'Grey Wolves (organization)'; Susurluk inquiry report, April 1997; Istanbul court verdict 12 Feb 2001
channels.drop_reason: The crash site is where the link surfaced, not a channel.

channels.n: Black Hand officers used Serbia's army for the Sarajevo plot: Belgrade → Sarajevo
channels.d: The Black Hand, a secret society of Serbian army officers, used its members' posts inside the army to organise killings. Its leader, Colonel Dragutin Dimitrijević ('Apis'), who had led the 1903 coup in which officers killed the king and queen, was made chief of the army's General Staff intelligence in 1913. Many scholars hold that he sanctioned the assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand: three young Bosnian Serbs were recruited, trained and smuggled from Serbia into Bosnia, with the Black Hand supplying weapons, and the killing on 28 June 1914 helped set off the First World War. His role is disputed. In 1917 he was court-martialled for treason and shot.
channels.cite: Wikipedia 'Black Hand (Serbia)'; Salonika court-martial 1917; Encyclopaedia Britannica
channels.drop_reason: The Sarajevo assassination is not infiltration.

channels.n: Gambian president's rosewood monopoly: Casamance → Banjul → China
channels.d: Westwood Company Ltd, the Gambian firm that held the exclusive licence to export rosewood, was co-founded by The Gambia's own president, Yahya Jammeh, with Swiss national Nicolae Bogdan Buzaianu, according to a 2019 complaint by the Swiss NGO TRIAL International; the president's office had awarded the licence to a company he part-owned. The rosewood was mostly logged in Senegal's Casamance region, trucked into The Gambia and shipped from Banjul. The Gambia exported about $163 million of rosewood to China in 2014–17, the Environmental Investigation Agency reported in 2020.
channels.cite: TRIAL International (2019); EIA 'Cashing in on Chaos' (2020)
channels.drop_reason: A leader's own business, not infiltration.

channels.n: Trilateral Commission members staffed Carter's government: New York → Washington
channels.d: The Trilateral Commission, a private forum of business and political figures from North America, Western Europe and Japan, was founded in 1973 at banker David Rockefeller's insistence, with Zbigniew Brzezinski as organiser. Jimmy Carter and Walter Mondale were members before they took office as President and Vice-President in 1977, and other members followed them into the administration. In April 1980 the Christian Science Monitor counted 21 former members holding posts in it, including Brzezinski as National Security Adviser and Harold Brown as Defense Secretary. The count is a newspaper's; no inquiry has examined whether the commission shaped the administration's decisions.
channels.drop_reason: Its organisation was removed under the Nov 2026 stricter test

channels.n: WEF Young Global Leaders who went on to lead governments
channels.d: The World Economic Forum (WEF), a Swiss foundation based in Cologny near Geneva and best known for its Davos meeting, works to shape government policy through cooperation between companies and states. Since 1992 it has picked rising politicians and business people, now under about 40, for a leadership network, today the Young Global Leaders, a five-year programme of meetings and courses. Alumni who later led governments include Justin Trudeau (Canada), Emmanuel Macron (France), Jacinda Ardern (New Zealand) and Sanna Marin (Finland); a 2021 paper by the German Bundestag's research service lists several of them. Membership is a WEF selection; no inquiry has found that the network directed their decisions.
channels.cite: Wikipedia 'Forum of Young Global Leaders'; Deutscher Bundestag, Wissenschaftliche Dienste, WD 1-3000-014/21 (2021)
channels.drop_reason: Its organisation was removed under the Nov 2026 stricter test

channels.n: US Fellowship network's Ugandan chair and the anti-gay bill: Washington → Kampala
channels.d: The Fellowship (also called The Family), a Washington-based Christian network that builds private ties with lawmakers through prayer groups and national prayer breakfasts, has a Ugandan arm chaired by politician David Bahati. Journalist Jeff Sharlet reported that Bahati first floated his 2009 Anti-Homosexuality Bill, which proposed the death penalty, at the 2008 Uganda National Prayer Breakfast. Fellowship member Bob Hunter confirmed Bahati's link to the network to NPR; a Fellowship member denied that its associates were behind the bill. In 2023 the Fellowship paid for a US congressman's keynote at Uganda's breakfast. Bahati has been a state minister since 2021.
channels.cite: Wikipedia 'The Fellowship (Christian organization)'; NPR, Dec 2009; Wikipedia 'David Bahati'
channels.drop_reason: Its organisation was removed under the Nov 2026 stricter test

channels.n: Russian agent Maria Butina into US political circles: Moscow → Washington
channels.d: Maria Butina, working under Russian official Alexander Torshin, built back channels for Russia into Republican circles in the United States through the National Rifle Association. The National Prayer Breakfast, an event run by the Christian network the Fellowship and attended by the president, served as a meeting place: she helped arrange Russian attendance in February 2017, and a planned private meeting between Torshin and President Trump was cancelled after a national security aide flagged him. Butina pleaded guilty on 13 December 2018 to conspiring to act as an undeclared agent of a foreign government and was sentenced to 18 months. The FBI interviewed Fellowship organiser Doug Burleigh about her.
channels.cite: Wikipedia 'The Fellowship (Christian organization)'; United States v. Maria Butina (D.D.C.), plea 13 Dec 2018, sentence 26 Apr 2019
channels.drop_reason: Its organisation was removed under the Nov 2026 stricter test

channels.n: Ford-funded Berkeley economists ran Suharto's economy
channels.d: The Ford Foundation, a large US private foundation, paid for economists from the University of Indonesia to take graduate degrees at the University of California, Berkeley from the late 1950s. After Suharto took power in 1966 he made them his economic team, later called the 'Berkeley Mafia': Widjojo Nitisastro headed the planning agency BAPPENAS from 1967 to 1983 and wrote Indonesia's Five-Year Development Plans, and Ali Wardhana was Finance Minister from 1968 to 1983. Their programme cut inflation and opened the country to foreign investors. The Ford Foundation describes its role in its own history, 'Celebrating Indonesia'.
channels.cite: Ford Foundation, 'Celebrating Indonesia'; Hill and Thee, Bulletin of Indonesian Economic Studies (2008)
channels.drop_reason: Its organisation was removed under the Nov 2026 stricter test

channels.n: US-funded 'Chicago Boys' took Pinochet's economic posts
channels.d: A US government aid scheme, later taken over by the Ford Foundation, linked the University of Chicago's economics department with Santiago's Catholic University and paid for 126 Chilean students to train under it between 1955 and 1973. Known as the 'Chicago Boys', its graduates wrote 'El ladrillo' ('The Brick'), the plan General Pinochet's military government adopted as its economic programme in 1975, and then held its economic posts: Sergio de Castro was economy and then finance minister, and Miguel Kast ran the planning office, the labour ministry and, from 1982, the Central Bank. The programme is described in Milton and Rose Friedman's memoir Two Lucky People (1998).
channels.cite: Wikipedia 'Chicago Boys'; Milton and Rose Friedman, Two Lucky People (1998)
channels.drop_reason: Its organisation was removed under the Nov 2026 stricter test

channels.n: Salvini aide sought secret Russian oil money for the Lega: Moscow → Milan
channels.d: Gianluca Savoini, a long-time aide of Lega leader Matteo Salvini and president of the Milan-based Lombardy–Russia cultural association, negotiated with Russian counterparts an oil deal meant to channel Russian money secretly to the Lega, then part of Italy's governing coalition. The talks took place at Moscow's Metropol hotel in October 2018 and were recorded; the recording was published in 2019. Milan prosecutors investigated Savoini and others for international corruption. In April 2023 a judge closed the case, finding the actions were 'unequivocally aimed' at illegal party financing but that the deal never got far enough to be a crime.
channels.drop_reason: Its organisation was removed under the Nov 2026 stricter test

channels.n: Dutch cocaine fugitive protected inside Sierra Leone's ruling circle
channels.d: Jos Leijdekkers ('Bolle Jos'), a Dutch fugitive sentenced in absentia in Rotterdam in 2024 to 24 years for smuggling over 7 tonnes of cocaine, has 'high-level protection' inside Sierra Leone's ruling circle, Reuters reported on 25 January 2025, citing three sources and video. Two sources said he is married to President Julius Maada Bio's daughter Agnes, and the footage shows him two rows behind the president at a New Year's Day mass. Dutch police had believed he was living in Turkey. Sierra Leone said it was investigating and dismissed its head of immigration; the government denies knowing where he is.
channels.drop_reason: Its organisation was removed under the Nov 2026 stricter test

patterns.title: Governments inside companies
patterns.summary:
Governments and their spy services get inside companies, both their own country's and other countries', to reach money, technology and the data of the people who use them. Some do it openly, through law and ownership. Others do it quietly, by placing or recruiting someone on the inside.

The open route is most developed in China, where the ruling party sits inside firms as a party cell, and it is written into law: any company with three or more Communist Party members must set up a party unit, and the party reported in 2018 that nearly three in four private firms had one, including the owner of TikTok.

The quiet route works through insiders, and the record shows it in the United States, Europe and Japan. Foreign intelligence officers and state talent programmes recruit engineers at aerospace, power and technology companies to carry out trade secrets; foreign officials have paid staff at a social-media company and a telephone company for users' data and network files; and a top manager of a large German payments firm was found to have worked with Russian intelligence. North Korea gets its programmers hired by foreign firms as remote workers under stolen identities and sends their wages to its weapons programmes; US prosecutors have found them placed in hundreds of American companies.

The longest-running case shows how far it can go: from 1970 the US CIA and West Germany's BND secretly owned Crypto AG, a Swiss company that sold cipher machines to more than 120 governments, and read those governments' coded messages for decades.

For customers and staff, this means a phone network, an app or an employer can be passing information to a government they never dealt with, and a company paying a remote programmer may be funding another state's weapons.

patterns.title: Criminal money inside banks and firms
patterns.summary:
Organised crime groups need ordinary businesses. A drug cartel or mafia has to turn cash into money it can spend, wants a share of public contracts, and has to move drugs through ports, airports and trucking firms. It gets what it needs in two ways: by owning companies through front men and investment funds, or by paying people already working inside a company who have the access it needs. Courts, prosecutors and sanctions records show both happening across Latin America, southern Europe, North America, East Asia and the big container ports of northern Europe.

Ownership can reach a whole industry. In Brazil, the PCC, a gang that began in São Paulo's prisons and now runs much of the country's drug trade, held a chain of investment funds that owned ethanol plants, a port terminal and more than a thousand petrol stations, investigators said in 2025. In Mexico and Italy, cartels and mafias own distilleries, building firms and security companies and bid for public works. Buying insiders is cheaper: bank staff who wave through suspicious transfers, terminal workers and IT contractors who hand over the codes that release a container, airport baggage handlers with passes to secure areas. An EU review in 2025 concluded that the loads of cocaine seized at European ports are too large to move without help from inside.

The cost falls on people who have nothing to do with the drug trade. Drivers buy fuel adulterated at stations a gang controls, commuters ride buses run by firms accused of laundering for one, and public money for rebuilding after a disaster goes to companies the mafia has taken over. In Japan, gang brokers placed workers in the state-funded Fukushima radiation clean-up and took part of their pay. When a bank used by launderers is shut, its ordinary customers may have to prove their own savings are clean to get them back. Some of this record rests on US Treasury sanctions, which are one government's decision rather than a court verdict.
patterns.uncertain: The PCC's holdings are what investigators said in 2025, not a court finding. Some cases rest on US Treasury sanctions, which are one government's decision rather than a court verdict.

patterns.title: Companies inside other companies
patterns.summary:
Companies, and the states that own or back them, get inside other companies to take their technology, win their contracts or control them through a front. The cases on this map run from Europe and North America to East Asia and the state-owned firms of Africa and Latin America, and they follow three methods.

The first is hidden ownership through a front. During the Second World War a Swedish bank held German companies on paper so their German owners kept control abroad.

The second is recruiting staff inside a rival or supplier, usually in high-technology industries such as chips and wind turbines, so that designs and code walk out of the door. When a Chinese turbine maker paid an engineer at its US supplier for control software, it stopped paying the supplier, which put its losses at more than US$800 million.

The third is paying managers of state-owned companies, such as national airlines, power utilities, oil firms and telecoms companies, to win their contracts. European engineering, telecoms, aerospace and oil-trading firms have admitted or been convicted of this in Indonesia, South Africa, Djibouti, Mexico, Ecuador and Brazil.

For workers, a stolen design can move the jobs and income built on it to another country. For taxpayers, a state company's manager paid by a supplier means the public pays more for its aircraft, power plants and phone networks. These cases came to light through prosecutions and company admissions.
patterns.uncertain: The figure of more than US$800 million in losses is the supplier's own estimate.

patterns.summary:
The bodies that set rules for many countries at once, such as the European Parliament, UN agencies, Interpol, the Council of Europe and the organisations that run world sport, are reached in the same ways as national governments. Governments and companies pay members for votes and statements, seat their own officials at the top, or place industry people inside national delegations. Because these bodies are far from voters and lightly policed, much of the record comes from foreign prosecutors, leaked papers and press investigations.

The European Parliament in Brussels has the densest record, with cases tied to Qatar, Morocco, Russia, China and the Chinese company Huawei. The clearest is the case Belgian prosecutors call Qatargate, in which they allege Qatar and Morocco paid people inside the Parliament, partly through a human-rights charity, after police found bags of cash at the home of one of its vice-presidents. In the Council of Europe's assembly of national MPs, an inquiry found Azerbaijani money had reached members who defended Azerbaijan's record.

Governments also seat their own officials in the top posts. Interpol, which circulates arrest requests between countries, has been led by a Chinese vice-minister of public security and then by a UAE interior ministry official, elected after the UAE gave its foundation about $54 million, reported to equal the yearly dues of every other member combined. Chinese officials have headed UN agencies for food and aviation, and the UN climate talks of 2023 and 2024 were led by figures from the hosts' oil industries.

Industries with most to lose work from inside the bodies that regulate them: tobacco companies against the WHO tobacco treaty, shipping groups inside delegations to the UN maritime agency, and sports-marketing firms and bid committees paying the officials who award tournaments and Olympic Games.

Decisions that reach everyone, such as climate targets, tobacco rules, cross-border arrest alerts, doping bans and war-crimes cases, can be shaped by the governments and companies they are meant to govern. People who fled a government may find its officials leading the body that handles arrest requests, and residents of EU countries live under laws that some of their representatives were paid to influence.

patterns.title: Banks and banking families
patterns.summary:
Banks reach into governments in two ways. Some pay officials or hide who owns them so that regulators and central banks look away. More often, and legally, bankers move into the posts that set financial policy and supervise banks, then move back. The cases on this map cover North and South America, Western Europe, the Gulf, Afghanistan and Malaysia.

The clearest case of the first kind is BCCI, the Bank of Credit and Commerce International, a Pakistani-founded bank closed worldwide for fraud in 1991. A US Senate inquiry found it had secretly owned Washington's largest bank through front owners, paid central bank officials in Latin America and hired former senators, prosecutors and regulators who helped slow the investigations. Smaller versions recur wherever a bank's owners are close to the ruling family, as with Kabul Bank in Afghanistan, part-owned by the president's and vice-president's brothers, which lost about $935 million to insiders.

The second kind is a career path between investment banks and the state. Former Goldman Sachs executives have run the US Treasury twice, led the central banks of Italy, Canada, Britain and the euro area, and become prime ministers of Italy and Canada. Argentina's economy ministry and central bank are run by former JPMorgan and Deutsche Bank executives, Germany's chancellor chaired BlackRock's German arm, and two French presidents came from the Rothschild bank. None of these moves has been found illegal.

The pattern is old: in 1910 senior Wall Street bankers met in secret to draft the plan for the US central bank. A popular claim that the Rothschilds or other Jewish banking families control governments and wars dates from the 1840s and is an antisemitic conspiracy theory; the Federal Reserve is run by a board appointed by the President and confirmed by the Senate.

When former bankers run economy ministries and central banks, decisions on debt, wages and bank rescues are made by people who know the lenders' side best. In the 2008 rescue of the insurer AIG, public money paid its trading partners in full, and in Malaysia and Afghanistan the public has paid for money taken by people close to power.
patterns.uncertain: No court or inquiry has found that the Rothschild bank directed the policies of the two French presidents who worked there, and no court has found the Goldman Sachs moves into government illegal.

patterns.title: Scam compounds and casino money inside Asian states
patterns.summary:
In parts of South-East Asia, companies that run online scams and gambling aimed at people in China and around the world have got their owners into local office or into the circle around national leaders. The scams are run from guarded compounds where trafficked workers are held and forced to defraud strangers online, and the political ties are what let the compounds operate in the open.

The pattern is clearest in Cambodia and the Philippines. In Cambodia, business figures tied to the compounds have held honorary titles, advisory posts and a seat in the Senate, and relatives of the ruling family have owned stakes in the payment firms the money passes through. In the Philippines, the state licensed Chinese-run offshore gambling firms from 2016, and some of them used local office-holders to set up and protect large compounds in provincial towns.

Three cases show the shape of it. Chen Zhi, who built the Prince Group into one of Cambodia's largest conglomerates and served as an official adviser to Hun Sen and other leaders, was indicted by the United States in 2025 as the head of a cyber-fraud business, and Cambodia later sent him to China. Huione Group, a Phnom Penh financial firm whose payment arm counted a cousin of Prime Minister Hun Manet among its owners and directors, was named by the US Treasury as having laundered over $4 billion. In the Philippines, Alice Guo, mayor of the town where a scam compound was raided, was found to be a Chinese citizen who could never lawfully hold office, and was jailed for life for human trafficking.

For the people trafficked into these compounds, and for their families, a mayor or a relative of the head of government standing near the business leaves few safe places to complain. For victims abroad, stolen savings can pass through payment firms owned by people close to power. The Philippines has since banned the industry and charged officials; in Cambodia most of the action so far has come from the United States, Britain and China rather than from Cambodian courts.
patterns.uncertain: The charges against Chen Zhi have not been tried. The US Treasury finding on Huione is an administrative decision by one government, not a court verdict.
patterns.drop_reason: Retired Nov 2026 after stricter case test: Only two cases remain (Alice Guo's mayoralty and the Manila airport 'pastillas' bribes), and the pattern's Cambodian core, Chen Zhi's adviser posts and the Huione ownership ties, rested on cases that were dropped.

patterns.title: French lodges and African presidencies
roles: Head of state or minister in a lodge
patterns.case_role: Head of state or minister in a lodge

countries.note: The Grande Loge Nationale Française and the Grand Orient de France sponsored or chartered lodges in former colonies; the GLNF's grand master installed Ali Bongo as grand master of Gabon's lodge in 2009. Jacques Foccart's Service d'Action Civique ran France's African networks from the Élysée.

patterns.summary:
Across the former French colonies of West and Central Africa, presidents and senior ministers have often belonged to Masonic lodges, many of them tied to lodges in France. Freemasonry is a lawful society whose members meet privately in lodges and swear oaths of mutual support; a grand lodge is the national body over them. In several of these countries the head of state has also been the head of the national grand lodge, so the same man leads the government and the private society that his ministers, police chiefs and senior officials belong to.

The habit of using lodges to steer appointments has roots in France itself, where in 1904 lodges of the Grand Orient, France's largest Masonic body, were found to have kept files on army officers that the war ministry used to decide promotions.

Gabon is the clearest example in Africa. Omar Bongo, president from 1967 to 2009, founded and led the country's lodges, and the head of a French grand lodge installed his son Ali as grand master in the same year Ali became president. The arrangement outlasted the 2023 coup that removed Ali Bongo: the lodges kept a state official as grand master, and the head of the Grand Orient reportedly met the coup leader in secret and offered support. Press reporting in France and Africa has named the presidents or senior ministers of Congo, the Central African Republic, Chad, Niger, Burkina Faso, Mali, Guinea, Côte d'Ivoire and Senegal as lodge members or lodge leaders. In Cameroon, Le Monde reported in 1999 that President Paul Biya paid tens of millions of francs to a French Templar order, part of it from the state oil company.

The arrangement is older than independence. In Liberia, lodge membership was treated as a requirement for leading the ruling party until the 1980 coup.

For citizens of these countries, it means a president and his ministers can settle matters in meetings that parliament and the press cannot attend, sometimes with French lodge leaders present. People cannot tell whether an appointment, a contract or French backing came through official channels or through lodge contacts. Ordinary lodge members are not accused of anything, and most of this record comes from press reports, not court cases.
patterns.uncertain: Most memberships rest on press reports, mainly Jeune Afrique in 2012, and several presidents have not confirmed them. No court has found that a lodge directed a government decision in these countries. Senegal's president Macky Sall denied the membership his opponents claimed. The Grand Orient leader's meeting with Gabon's coup leader is known from press reports.

confirmed_by.title: Jeune Afrique, investigation of Freemasonry in Africa, 2012
Le Monde, 1999, on payments to the Ordre Souverain du Temple Initiatique

patterns.drop_reason: Retired Nov 2026 after stricter case test: Only one case remains (the 1904 French officers' files affair), and the pattern's premise, that African presidents and ministers belonged to or led Masonic lodges, rested on membership cases that were cut because nothing showed the lodges steered decisions through them.

patterns.title: Lenders, aid programmes and trained technocrats
roles: Country whose economy was run by the trainees or advisers
patterns.case_role: Country whose economy was run by the trainees or advisers

countries.note: The Ford Foundation paid for Indonesian economists to train at Berkeley; the US aid agency (ICA, later USAID) funded the 1956 agreement between the University of Chicago and Chile's Catholic University; the US Treasury ran the Saudi Joint Commission from a Saudi-funded trust account.

patterns.summary:
From the 1950s to the 1980s, US government aid and the Ford Foundation, an American private foundation, paid for economists from poorer countries to take degrees at American universities. Some of those graduates later ran their own countries' economies under military governments, bringing the thinking of the schools that trained them into the ministries that set budgets, taxes, borrowing and interest rates. The record on this map covers Chile and Indonesia.

The method was slow and indirect. Money paid for a link between a US university and a local one, students went abroad for years, and when a general seized power and wanted a ready-made economic team, the graduates were there with a plan. In Chile, economists trained at the University of Chicago, known as the 'Chicago Boys', wrote the economic programme that General Pinochet's government adopted in 1975 and then held the economy and finance ministries and the central bank until the 1982 debt crisis. In Indonesia, economists trained at the University of California, Berkeley, later called the 'Berkeley Mafia', became General Suharto's economic team after 1966 and ran planning and finance for well over a decade.

This is not bribery or spying. The outside money paid for training years before anyone took office, and the governments that appointed these men chose them freely. What it produced was a small group, trained on foreign money and sharing one school's ideas, that wrote national economic policy for more than a decade in each country.

For people in Chile and Indonesia, it meant living under economic plans drawn up by officials they had not elected, appointed by generals who had taken power by force. When those plans worked, as Indonesia's did against runaway inflation in the late 1960s, the public had no voice in them, and when they failed, as Chile's did in the 1982 debt crisis, people bore the cost without having been asked.
patterns.uncertain: The link between foreign-funded training and the policies these men wrote is an inference; the governments that appointed them chose them freely.

confirmed_by.title: US General Accounting Office report on the US–Saudi Arabian Joint Commission on Economic Cooperation, 1979
New York Times, 'Economic Hit Man' review, 2005

patterns.drop_reason: Retired Nov 2026 after stricter case test: No cases remain. The Chile and Indonesia economists were trained on foreign money but appointed freely by their own governments, which the new test treats as open outside action, not infiltration.

patterns.summary:
The people who run a country's treasury, central bank and financial regulators are often drawn straight from the banks, investment funds and international lenders they then oversee or negotiate with. Some return to finance afterwards. The pattern is clearest in the United States, France and Germany, but it is found on every continent, and in poorer countries the same move runs from the IMF or World Bank into the finance ministry.

In the United States it goes back to the founding of the Federal Reserve, whose plan bankers drafted at Jekyll Island in 1910 and whose first board included a Kuhn, Loeb partner. Since then Treasury secretaries and bank regulators have come from Citigroup, Goldman Sachs, Carlyle and hedge funds, and in 2020 the Federal Reserve hired BlackRock to run its emergency bond buying. In France two leaders came from the Rothschild bank, and Germany's chancellor chaired BlackRock's German arm. Lebanon's central bank was run for 30 years by Riad Salameh, a former Merrill Lynch banker who had managed the prime minister's personal portfolio.

Where a country is in debt, the move often comes from the lender itself. World Bank and IMF officials have been made finance minister, central bank governor or head of government in Pakistan, Nigeria, Indonesia, Turkey, Côte d'Ivoire and Panama, often during a financial crisis and while the country was negotiating a loan.

For people in these countries, it means that decisions on bank bailouts, interest rates, privatisation and debt are taken by people whose careers, contacts and in some cases shareholdings lie with the creditors and banks on the other side. Spain's bank bailout was run by the former head of Lehman Brothers' Spanish arm, and a US Federal Reserve official who came from the Carlyle private-equity firm eased oversight of mid-sized banks such as Silicon Valley Bank before it failed.
patterns.uncertain: Moving from a bank to a public post is legal and common, and supporters argue it brings needed skill; the cases here show the move, not that any official acted for a former employer. Some, such as Salameh in Lebanon, face criminal charges that are still before the courts. Claims drawn from Carroll Quigley's histories about Morgan and Lazard men in Washington rest on his reading of the period and are not universally accepted.
patterns.drop_reason: Retired Nov 2026 after stricter case test: Only three cases remain, and the pattern's premise was the move of bankers into public posts in itself, which the stricter test cut; its own caveat says the cases show the move, not that any official acted for a former employer. The remaining cases are better read under other patterns.
